review_date: Reviewed in the United States on July 20, 2025
review_body: Very pleased with this guitar. Tone is nice. Action is low (a consistent height of strings above frets) which makes the pressing of nylon strings comfortable. The action is adjustable since it has a truss rod and included allen wrench but I don't need to adjust it. Also included is a guitar case, clip-on tuner, capo, picks, extra strings, strap, cleaning cloth, and a footstool. I was surprised to see how accurate the tuner is and how easily I could tune the guitar. More surprisingly, I'm pleased with how long the guitar stays in tune. The tuner was not just for guitars. It is for chromatic, guitar, bass, violin, and Ukulele tuning. I’ve used it to tune my B-flat trumpet. Pitch range is listed at 440Hz.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2024
review_body: I've owned several different classical guitars ranging from $150 "cheapos" up to mid-level student guitars ( Yairi CY118 and Takamini Hirade ). I can say this is a very nice guitar for what I paid for it! I've owned a couple of inexpensive Yamahas and I want to say my last model was a c40 if memory serves me and this is every bit as nice and honestly a little bit nicer than that one. Fit and finish are good, the frets are finished well with no sharp edges and it has a nice laquer job. It has a warm and balanced tone and while not the loudest guitar it's loud enough for practicing or playing in small groups if you have decent acoustics in the room. Actions nice and low over the first fret and a tad high over the 12th fret but interestingly enough its not difficult at all to play, the strings are very easy to push down and I'm not going to even tamper with it, I usually shave down my saddles to lower the action but this one won't be needing it. I went ahead and ordered a set of diadario ej45s but honestly the strings that came with it sound pretty darn good so I'm not in a hurry to change them out. It also came with the bag tuner, footrest etc. normally I don't care about stuff like that but the accessories seem like decent quality and I will use them. Overall for the price you really can't beat this instrument and if you're trying to decide between something like this or one of the Yamahas for an inexpensive guitar or for a student don't be afraid to give this one a shot, I don't think you'll be disappointed. Hope this helps.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on December 9, 2025
review_body: This is the best amp I have owned. It sounds glorious and looks beautiful. I don't use the app much but it allows a lot of tone tweaking. Downloading a large number of tones is a big plus. I have an old VOX DA5 which has no app and sounds anemic in large spaces but sounds very good in small spaces. I also have a Spark 2 which is very good and has many decent tones, especially with AI engine, but doesn't come even close to THR30ii. While this one is almost twice the price of Spark 2, I would recommend it over spark 2 any day. What THR cannot easily do that Spark 2 can is to create tones by just telling it - "give me a Ken Burrell tone from Midnight blue" gives something that is close enough. And despite not having an AI capability like Spark 2 has, I prefer this amp for its tone and sound. The feature I have used is to download tones (I think there are 40 or so tones) and save them on the amp. Those tones are all better sounding than Spark 2 tones. Also, the bluetooth audio capability in this is far superior to Spark 2 which sometimes distorts sound. I suspect that as I use Spark 2 in a big city where airwaves might be saturated with wifi and bluetooth signals I have experienced some connection issues on Spark 2. I use THR30ii in a place where there is zero bluetooth and wifi density and that is why I have never experienced any connection problems. Overall, I would highly recommend this amp.

So I went on the hunt for something as easy as possible to use and it sound good. The Yamaha THR II 30 exceeded my expectations in every way possible. It takes me 5 seconds to turn this on and get great tone, the fact it's battery powered means I can go where my family is not. The wireless dongle you buy separately makes the unit completely wireless and is worth the 100 dollars. Then there is the tone, this thing sounds incredible and is very easy to tweak. I don't even need to use my Firehawk pedal anymore. Buying this has lead me to play guitar more because if I have 5 minutes, I can play still. Vs. before where it would take 30 minutes just to set up.

review_body: This is the perfect little home practice amp, especially if you get the wireless bug for your guitar. It is a bit expensive, considering that for the same money, you could buy a big, powerfull amp that you could play gigs with, but as convenient as this little amp is, I dont have a single regret about spending the money to buy it, and if I were ever so inclined, the line-outs on it could be used to plug into something big enough for a gig setting.

review_title: Pretty Good Beginner Guitar That’s Fun For Any Skill Level
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2024
review_body: So I really like this guitar! It has a hard plastic (or something similar) body that feels very solid and feels like it will last a long time as well. It has a really deep resonate tone as well. I chose the 30” version because I also have a KALA Baritone Ukelele and a Yamaha Guitalele. This one is pretty close in size to the KALA Baritone Uke, and quite a bit bigger than the Guitalele. But it sounds very much as loud and deep as a standard sized guitar. Its nylon strings are comfortable on the fingers and the neck is straight and overall is pretty well setup. My main concern with it is that the action is just too high to easily play. I can’t imagine how a novice would enjoy playing this. It takes a different amount of pressure to fret a note at the first fret than it does at the 12th. Or the 5th even. Or the 2nd actually. My plan is to lower the action at the bridge. The string height at the first fret/nut is actually reall good. I have some (a little) experience working on banjos and the “repair” I have to perform is fairly minimal. Even so, I have the proper tools to modify the bridge and to accurately measure the action as I go along. So I feel very comfortable making this change.

review_title: Very well made child's musical instrument. Holds its tune, unlike other small beginner guitars.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on April 6, 2024
review_body: Very pleased with this guitar that is very well made. It includes the truss and truss adjustment that stabilizes the neck against the stretch of the guitar strings, so that it holds its tune. It is a musical instrument - not a frustrating toy for a beginning learner. The included tuner works for all of the notes. This was not so for a competitor we purchased and returned since it was poorly made and didn't hold a tune at all!) I ordered replacement strings from a music store, since another reviewer suggested that. But, so far we are happy with the strings that it came with. After buying the cheaper one, I delved further into research for a child's guitar and found this was recommended by a true guitar manufacturer. A big brand name was twice the cost or more, which wasn't reasonable for what may be a passing interest for our grandchild. It is not a small "parlor" guitar for an adult, but has the smaller neck and fret length for small child's hands. Very nice tone given the small size. We have not used the online lessons, since we will let our son set that up but that's a nice extra.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on April 2, 2025
review_body: This 1/4 size guitar is nice quality for young beginners to learn on. It is a scaled down version of a full size guitar and I like that it doesn’t make any compromises on components. Many beginner guitars have plastic or otherwise cheap feeling parts, they don’t hold a tune and don’t sound terrific. This guitar feels great in hand and sounds warm and really nice. It has nylon strings which are more beginner friendly than metal ones, being more comfortable to play. They take a couple more days to break in but hold tune just fine after that. The guitar comes with an extra set of strings which is handy. Overall a nice guitar for little kids to learn on before they can handle a full or even half size guitar.

review_body: I have 3 Enya caron fiber guitars and I love all of them. Most recently I bought the NOVA GO SP1 acoustic which I will say I had reservations with, I was a little hesitant about its durability, size and how it would sound, but all for naught as it doesn’t dissapoint in build quality, appearance or sound characteristics. I had been learning to play, on and off for quite a few years, sometimes ardently commited to it, other times half heartedly, but always loving the instrument and loving to “play”. Regardless of if I was any good at it, after all, the only one I had to please or entertain was myself. I was finally getting to a point where I was feeling confident, like I was finally “getting it” when unfortunately, at about that same time, I developed a health condition which caused me chronic pain and to become fatigued very quickly. The weight and size of my guitars was intolerable, so I begrudginly had to give it up completely. I am so grateful to have recently seen these carbon fiber guitars on Amazon, I was intrigued by the positive reviews and all the comments regarding their weight and convenience. I figured I would give them a try even with my low stamina and back pain issues. I started with the XMari and loved it, then the Go Sonic, loved that too, and now the SP1. Enya hit the trifecta on these, the light weight and convenience have allowed me to pick up the thing I loved so much again and the excellent quality of the looks, construction, functionallity and sound is the icing on the cake. I would reccomend these to anyone, from beginner or hobbyist to seasoned pro. I can’t say enough good about all of the Enya products, the kind of quality and value that is a rarity in todays world.

review_body: I was never a great guitar player but I used to be good at improving melodies and finishes to existing songs. That was in my youth, when I played. Now that I am retiring in January, I want to relearn guitar and take a swing at composition. I am medium statured with not so big hands, so I require a quality slimline, left handed guitar, which many know are nearly impossible to find. I originally considered a Godin A6 Ultra, but the humidity here in Wyoming gets down to 0%, and I didn't want a $2,000 guitar to crack in a few months. I was going to split the difference with a Fender Acoustasonic, but they no longer make that for lefties. This Ibanez is perfect! It is slim profile, light weight, and it has a thin neck but enough frets to do the job. I don't need for it to produce performance level sound. I just want to be able to pick it up and compose without plugging it into an amp. Of course, having the ability to plug it into an amp is a plus for when I want to record. It's not the best guitar, but the sound quality is there, it is for lefties, and the price point can't be beat!

review_title: A well designed highly portable travel/practice guitar.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on April 6, 2025
review_body: This will fit in an airline overhead. Mine fits (without the gig bag) diagonally in my 25” roller suitcase. It is quiet enough for a hotel room. I can play it in the den while my wife watches TV. It is full scale (on the long side) so it is good for practice. It sounds great with my Vox amped headset. The quality is good. It buzzed at first but I cured that with a truss rod adjustment (included wrench). The action is good. If your goal is a practice guitar on the road or if others are nearby, it’s a great choice. I wouldn’t use it as a performance guitar though it might work with a small speaker/amp but it doesn’t have the resonance of a “real” guitar. For the reason I bought it - quiet practice and portability - I’d totally buy it again. I think the price is reasonable given the quality.

review_body: It's not only for acoustics -- I use the THR5A as a home/practice amp for my electric guitar. Since I play only in a jazz style and hate overdrive distortion, the amp works really well. I don't use the recommended "EG Clean" setting; I use the "Condenser Mic" setting, which gives just the right tone for jazz guitar by helping to preserve the acoustic sonorities of my archtop while at the same time amplifying them. And when I play with a Stratocaster it gives roughly the same effect, creating the illusion that the Strat is a hollow-body -- great for guitaring with headphones while others are sleeping. (When you set it to "EG Clean" the "Blend" knob becomes a gain knob, so you can get a bit of overdrive that way. Works okay; I simply don't play in that style.)

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on September 21, 2015
review_body: I'm using this primarily for ukulele. And wow *THIS* is it. I'd tried a few before arriving at this little gem of an amp. What I was looking for was a decent acoustic practice amp for home or small groups that was portable and could take batteries. I tried the Blackstar Fly3 but it was just not as clean sounding - I could get close just using my electric guitar Vox 10 amp if I tweaked the settings enough. So I came across the THR series of amps and decided to give the THR10C a try which is geared towards Jazz thinking the cleaner output would lend itself well to nylon. It's a really nice amp but still too electric sounding. That's when I discovered they made a acoustic specific amp, this THR5A. Not only does it have a "nylon" specific setting (which I actually do not play in all of the time), but it has mic models rather than amp models. There is a mixer that blends straight pickup with the mic model. And if you wanna get a little funky, it also has some reverb and hall effect. The compression effect is great to tighten up the sound on strumming so it sounds cleaner. The big thing missing from its THR10 cousins is the ability to memorize settings but I'm ok with that. Also, I understand that the THR5 series puts out the same power as the THR10 series which I was afraid coming from the 10C I would give up some volume but not the case.

review_title: UPDATED 3/6/2022: READ ME! Not as bad as people say! people just love to complain.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on May 3, 2021
reviewer_name: College Guy trying to be helpful :)
review_body: READ THIS IF YOU'RE CONSIDERING BUYING THIS GUITAR!!! I bought this used - very good for 45 bucks about a year ago. I probably would not pay full price, as much as I love it. That being said, IT IS NOT JUNK GIVE IT TIME! I swear half the people leaving negative reviews have no idea how guitars work. I am a full grown adult guitar player, and I've been playing since high school. I'm in college now, and I needed something small and light to travel with. I DON'T USE THIS AS MY EVERYDAY GUITAR! I reach for this guy if I'm messing around with chords, my fingers hurt from my metal strings, or I'm just trying to relax. It's great to practice on, but not so much if you're trying to actually play in front of people. Nylons aren't meant to be used like metal stringed acoustics, they're a separate instrument! It still works for that purpose, though, you can play the same exact songs and chords. If you tune it properly it gets the job done. Great for my college dorm or throwing in the car for a camping trip cus it's super light. Great to practice on when I don't feel like lugging my full sized acoustic around. This is a decent product for the price I PAID. Being a nylon string guitar, you have to stretch the strings and tune it quite a bit (2-4 days is recommended for the strings to settle - watch a youtube tutorial on how to do it) Furthermore, the plastic strings that everyone complains about are standard on a nylon. Heck, the C40 from Yamaha, well established nylon, has the same type (but higher quality, I bet) if I recall. They do go out of tune pretty frequently, especially at the start, but it's not even that much - just retune them! The tuner works well for me, but if you don't like it, just get an app like GuitarTuna. Now, for the guitar itself, it's what I expected when I bought it for 45 bucks, barely even damaged since I got a higher quality used (or less damaged I guess) version, and I have to say, it has really grown on me. Guitars are instruments, not toys. You can't give it to a kid and expect them to learn the ins and outs. If you really want them to learn guitar, buy them a cheap acoustic like a rogue or Yamaha, a C40 is a great nylon but you could also get them a metal string, and get them lessons! Find a music store near you, it might be a bit pricey but it's the best way to learn. Originally I recommended swapping the strings, but it's not worth it to be honest. I got it back in 2021 for 45 USD used, and I love it for what I use it for. If you're dead-set on a cheap starter guitar, or you want an affordable spare, grab this but follow my advice. If you really want to learn, shell out the extra money and buy a tried and true brand. For the full price, 80 bucks is not worth it. Get a rogue for that money. Anyway, that's my rant, hope this helps! (I even bumped my review up from 4 to 5 stars - when I first wrote it, it was 1 star because I didn't understand stretching the nylon strings - IT TAKES TIME! but I genuinely love this thing!) Enjoy!

review_title: Great Guitar For The Price - Here's What You Need To Know
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 8, 2021
review_body: I've wanted a guitar for pretty much my entire life. I've always been unable to get one because of either lack of money, or not being able to find a good one. When I found this guitar, after a LONG time of looking everywhere on the internet, I knew that I had to buy it. The reviews were good, sure maybe some were iffy, but overall it looked great. It just arrived today, and I'm genuinely SHOCKED at how good it looks. It's polished, has three steel strings and three nylon strings (which I'll talk about later), comes with a digital clip-on tuner, guitar pick, replacement strings and a guitar strap. I'm 5'-5'1 and this guitar is the PERFECT size for me. It's not too small, and not too big (although a little bigger than I expected but that's a good thing because I wasn't sure if it'd be too small for me or not). There are a few cons to this guitar, mainly the fact that the guitar strap doesn't really attach. It has a knob at the bottom of the guitar that you can attach it to but then the instructions direct you to just tie it around the headstock, and that's not really how you're supposed to attach a guitar strap (I mean, I'm pretty sure anyway). I personally don't really need the strap anyways, but if that's a major thing for you that might be a bit of a problem. Other than that, it does look a tiny bit...dinged up? I'm not sure if that's the word for it, but if you look really closely at all the details around the fretboard, it looks a bit scratched up. It doesn't affect the overall beauty of the instrument nor the sound of it, so that's not really a big deal for me but I thought I'd include it in my review for honesty's sake. The problem I do have with this guitar though, is that the nylon strings are VERY loose. I'm not sure if that's just a mistake on my part or what, because frankly this is my first guitar and I'm really not sure if I tuned it correctly (probably not), but I have been told the strings should be okay how they are? Apparently nylon strings are supposed to be looser. Other than that, this is a great instrument and I would 100% recommend buying this if you're looking for a budget guitar. It's not super pricey, it sounds great, and looks beautiful. (I named my guitar Anastasia by the way, she's gorgeous, see the attached picture!)

review_title: Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 31, 2026
review_body: I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 9, 2023
review_body: 69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 23, 2026
review_body: Initially ordered a size 6. I did an exchange for a 6.5Wide as it provides more wiggle room. I do not like very tight shoes. the 6 was way too tight for me. they are easy to slip on/off, the soles are thicker than what i prefer, but they are NOT platform style soles, so they should work fine, it is SUPPORT! (avid 25+ year Converse All Star wearer here). they seem to have excellent traction, i've only worn them out once (after i received my exchanged pair) and it was a comfy walk on dry sidewalk. the shoe quality seems to be good, i have noticed a few frayed threads sticking out, but honestly, i do not care. i dislike wearing shoes inside my home, especially on a top floor apartment (noise to neighbors, yes im nice and do everything to prevent heavy walking), but recently have an issue with tendonitis in one foot. OBVIOUSLY from my chucks and getting older and how i walk around at home lol, but listen, I wore these inside for a hour and hardly any noise, i felt floaty... normally I just slide around in socks. OVERALL: the wearability seems on point, I don't have any complaints yet. they are for work where I will be on concrete all day. I already know these will help. I can't really say HOW to choose your size, just do the research and buy a pair with the idea- you may have to exchange for a different size, and with that said- DO NOT LOSE THE TAGS (i removed mine from shoes but kept in great condition inside box for the return), DO NOT WALK OUTSIDE, KEEP EVERYTHING IN GOOD CONDITION- IN CASE- you have to do an exchange. They're worth the money, I honestly believe so and I don't like any shoe but converse all-stars. oh, and they send you an extra set of longer laces which i prefer. hope this helps anyone :)

It has been applied to so many different products out there in the market (not just these items) such as meds/drugs (they all mention that results may vary), or gasoline usage per mile can also vary,…I am just a regular consumer/shopper. review_title: Level of fragrance really depends on the type of candle you choose!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 12, 2018
review_body: Have ordered 2 of these candles - the Peace + Tranquility (white) and the Reflection + Clarity (light blue). Both were excellent, but the Peace + Tranquility definitely had a lighter aroma / more subtle than the Reflection + Clarity. Saw several reviews stating they couldn't smell the candle. There are 2 likely reasons - 1: if you have a large room/house that you want to smell the candle in, I highly recommend the coffee table jar, which has 3 wicks and smells much stronger than the single wick candles. However, since it has three wicks, it does burn through faster. I light mine every night for a couple of hours after dinner while I clean the kitchen and they each lasted about 2-3 weeks with nightly use. Secondly, it definitely seems to vary with the the fragrance type you use. The Peace + Tranquility is very light and fresh smelling, but not at all strong. The Reflection + Clarity is very strong and pleasant, it kind of smells like laundry detergent though (this can be a good or bad thing depending on how you feel about your laundry detergent!). I have a large house with high ceilings and you can smell the Reflection + Clarity everywhere after being lit 30 minutes or so. I like to use the R+C type of I make a very strong-smelling dinner (with lots of garlic or onions) where I want to refresh the house. I use the P+T when I just want a nice calm scent. I will definitely order again, but will probably try another couple of types since they seem to vary quite a bit...

review_body: One of the best tennis shoes I’ve ever owned! I’m big into exercise and love walking. I aim for 20k-30k steps per day and a lot of that comes from treadmill walking when I’m not hiking. With treadmill walking I definitely need a supportive shoe that still has great cushioning or I get crazy foot cramps. I also just slightly overpronate and old injuries cause my feet to swell a bit. I also have sacroiliac joint pain so I need shoes that help lower back pain and alignment; it’s not crazy bad but something that cheap unsupportive shoes aggravate. I used to swear by AS!CS GT 2000 models but the last few releases have been so uncomfortable. I also heard great things about Brooks so I did some research and decided to invest in these. I’m glad I did because these fit every need. They’re beyond comfortable; the insole reminds me of Clark’s Cloudstepper shoes which are crazy comfortable just these have more targeted support and recovery. My back feels better, my feet swell less, and my persistent foot cramps are probably 95% better. The fit is great, roomy in the toe box so no pinching, I don’t have wide feet but I dislike if my toes feel cramped. I’d say these maybe run just a hair big. Size is my go to size for tennis shoes but it generally takes a few weeks of wear to scratch the shoe a bit for that size to feel perfect. These size 7s fit out of the box like I’ve had those few weeks of wear; which is great as long as they don’t stretch more. I’ve worn them for about a week and they haven’t really stretched so I think the size will remain fine. However if you’re between sizes I’d maybe recommend sizing down instead of the normal size up rule with tennis shoes. These are expensive shoes but for me they’re 100% worth it and I will purchase again when I need a new pair; they seem durable so hopefully they’ll last longer than most shoes. Highly highly recommend especially for anyone with foot and back pain or for anyone who puts a lot of miles on their shoes. Bonus I normally don’t run because of foot pain but jogging on the treadmill actually felt good in these so I’d say great for runners too!

review_title: This shirt is comfortable and does not shrink very much
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on December 30, 2021
review_body: This is an excellent shirt for a bargain price, especially when bought in the 10-pack. There are no side seams to itch you. The back neck and shoulders are covered in fabric which is not always the case in undershirts. The front neck, armholes, cuffs, sleeve seams, and bottom hem are not fabric covered, but they are surged with a very soft thread which is much more comfortable than the surging in some of my other shirts that scratches and itches my skin. I was worried that the crew neck would annoy me since I don't like anything tight around my neck, but it is loose enough that I can get it over my head with my glasses on, plus you can stretch it a little both ways when the shirt is wet. The cotton in this shirt is soft and surprisingly heavy, not like a typical men's undershirt. It is more an outer shirt than an undershirt, but it could be worn under a roomy outer shirt. It has cuffs, which is a very nice feature especially if the sleeves are a little long on someone. The weight and texture of the shirt seems to be between a tee shirt and a very light weight sweatshirt. I am using one for sleeping and it feels soft against my face at night and keeps me warm but not hot. The arms are long on me which I expected since I am only 5 feet 4 inches tall and I ordered the size large shirt. The size chart indicated I should order a medium or even a small if I wanted a snug shirt, but I went with the large for the comfort and I'm happy with the roominess. The sleeve width is roomy enough on me, but not too roomy. The construction of this shirt is excellent, in fact perfect except for a thread or two that was not cut off. I bought my shirts in the 10-pack and they arrived with all ten shirts ironed and folded in half neatly, all in one big plastic bag loosely taped shut and inside a big box. I didn't have a problem with the fact that each shirt was not individually wrapped, and in fact I can use the big plastic bag. Some reviewers said there were holes, unsewn seams and stains on their shirts, but mine were all in perfect new condition. I washed them and dried them in the dryer, but they do take a very long time to dry. I ended up hanging them up to complete the drying. The only negative thing I can say about this excellent shirt is that it has two very annoying scratchy tags sewn right into the back neck seam. You can't tear them off without ripping the stitches. I cut them out very carefully with tiny scissors. Here are the approximate dimensions of size large after washing and drying: underarm sleeve length 23", sleeve circumference at shoulder 20.5", sleeve circumference at middle of sleeve 15", back width at top between sleeve seams 20.25", circumference around the bottom 45.5", length at back middle 29".

review_body: I don't know what kind of mad scientist they have working for Owala, but can we get this guy working on improving other things, like those gas pumps that always shut off every $.05 cents, or maybe invent a cell phone screen protector that doesn't crack a week after you put it on? Seriously, what an amazing design they have. I love the Owala spouts. I detest water bottles with straws, except for Owala. These things are so pleasant to drink out of. Also, this lid is fantastic, it's leak proof, easy to remove (Stanley, take a look, this is better), and that little string loop thing goes great over your middle finger. That's the strongest point, and if someone messes with you swing that thing like a club! Seriously, don't go around just hitting people, but as a self-defense item this will work! It kept my ice water nice and cold today. They claim you can put other stuff in here, but really, why would you? It's such a fantastic water bottle. I guess if you wanted to load it up with coffee, tea, soda, or any number of adult beverages that's up to you. I just don't want to stain up the inside. The 18 ounce fits perfectly in my backpack's water bottle pocket. I have the Bellroy Transit Workpack Pro 28L. I bought this to take with me when I fly. Empty water bottles are allowed thru security, then fill it up after going through security. It'll save you a bunch on bottled water. If you want something easy to carry, fits any cup holder, and can hold enough water to quench your thirst for a reasonable amount of time the 18 ounce is perfect. If you're one of those people that likes to carry enough water for a full day of hiking on the AT this probably isn't for you. For the rest of us it's perfect! Great job Owala!

review_title: You can't go wrong with an Owala FreeSip bottle!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on October 12, 2025
review_body: I'm a big fan of Owala especially their FreeSip spout bottles. I already have the original design in the 24oz and 32oz, I also have the Sway in 40oz and now I was looking for a smaller bottle that is easier to travel with and this FreeSip Twist 18oz is the one! I do have to get used to the twist off cap that's not attached to the bottle since it's not as quick or easy to use as a push button attached lid. It is leak proof as advertised but beware that if you have ice water in your bottle and you have it laying on its side, the cap and right at the fill to area will form condensation (just like the other Owala bottles). I also like how this bottle can carry carbonated or hot liquids (the other Owalas do not recommend it). It is fairly easy to take apart and clean but coming from larger bottles where I can usually fit my hand in it to clean, this one you definitely need to invest in a bottle cleaning brush if you don't have one already. I hope Owala doesn't come out with other styles of FreeSip bottles because I'm just going to keep growing my collection! I love this Dreamy Fields color which seems to only be available through Amazon, it's a very subtle pink to the point where it looks almost white online but when placed next to my Shy Marshmallow (white bottle), you can clearly see the difference. I do wish Owala made a bottle boot that would fit this bottle, I ordered a generic one but it is just slightly too loose but it is still better than nothing since I don't want to scratch or dent the bottom of the bottle (btw, the Owala boots are the best quality ones you can get). The thin shape of this bottle is easy to grab and it does fit in the side pocket of my Baggallini Securetex Vacation backpack purse (you can look it up for reference) and it fits inside of that bag too (that's why I opted for the 18oz vs the 24oz one). The quality is great as usual and it does keep ice water cold for a long time. I do think that Amazon should improve the packaging on this type of item because it was shipped in the brown paper bag that no longer has any type of cushioning and this is a stainless steel bottle so I'm surprised and grateful that there were no dents or scratches when I received it (especially when I saw the delivery guy just throw the package onto my cement stairs). I did order multiple items hoping it would ship in 1 box but it was shipped separately on its own (my other items did come in a box).

review_title: Falls short to Yeti but still nice!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on July 29, 2025
review_body: I wanted this Stanley to be my reason to turn away from Yeti. I love the modern design, the all black, the non-fixed handle that can be tightened to be more fixed/harder to move, and the 50 oz capacity. It was nice to see that the bottle had 4 extra oz of capacity at the same price as Yeti’s 46 oz bottle. I need to drink lots of water throughout the day and the large capacity is awesome. The lightness was originally a selling point for me; while it can hold an astonishingly large 50 oz, since the bottle is relatively light in weight, it doesn’t feel too heavy to carry a full bottle around. However, where it excels in lightness it falls short in quality. It is glaringly lower quality than Yeti’s 46 oz bottle. This Stanley has thinner metal leading to poorer insulation. What frustrated me the most was realizing how much thinner the coating was compared to Yeti; I accidentally dinged it with a fork while heating up my lunch and chipped it! I’ve dropped my Yetis dozens of times and hit them with everything from forks and knives to granite countertops and haven’t had an issue with them chipping under light use. I even noticed it will take on light scratches from the plastic buckles on my lunch box if I let them touch while in my bag. Seriously poor coating. However, getting back to the pros, the leak resistance is great and when properly closed you can rest assured you won’t have spillage or leakage. Also the straw on this bottle is much nicer than the straws on Yeti bottles; less resistance and simply easier to sip. In the end, it’s a great water bottle that has a cool modern look and a huge capacity. Overall this comes in at 4/5 stars with only one star being lost to the thinner metal and thinner coating. I would still suggest getting the Yeti 46 oz instead for the thicker metal and coating as it will likely last longer and endure more.

I wanted to test it out because I know there’s some mixed reviews. I myself do not use ice in my drinks. I just use cold water so the ice retention for me is really not huge on whether I buy a bottle or not.. and let’s face it if you put water and ice into any water bottle you’re gonna have some weight, but I don’t think it’s that heavy and I have arthritis and some other issues. I love the handle on the sway. I don’t usually like cups that have the side handle. I just find those to be bulky, but I love the handle on the sway because even though I have small hands, sometimes I have to carry it versus putting it into my bag because I have a lot of things as being a teacher if you know you know. So I’m an advocate for cleaning your entire bottle and when I say entire bottle I mean take the little part and I don’t like 1 million gazillion pieces and I’m one that’s very thorough. I don’t just take a little brush through it. I take the seals off I take my watch a video first on it on TikTok and then because sometimes I don’t know how to clean the bottle lid and then of course I repeat that and I find this one to be extremely easy to clean even the piece that sits in the lid. I don’t know depend on the color you get mine is gray. I will just pop that out, clean it with the brush clean it however let it dry then put it all back together so you don’t get any type of mold because any water bottle you have you’re gonna have mold if you don’t clean your bottle and again I love this bottle and I did purchase it with my own money as I have no deal with them at all I’m not even vine reviewer( I wish).

My other water bottles have developed buildup in the cap/lid that result in black mold. Regardless of how much and how well I clean them, they never seem clean and the build up is in tiny/dark crevices that are hard to reach. The rubber stopper comes out easily to clean or replace as needed and prevents spills. The snap right straw cover works perfectly and even has a locking mechanism. I held out this long because I love GLOSSY screens and they are impossible to get from a major manufacturer today. Looking online at this monitor, I made a judgement that the anti-glare is similar to TV models and nowhere as terrible as Dell's 3H hardcoat AG coating...it's like looking at the monitor through a viel/stocking, terrible! Imagine going through life with a stocking over your head because the market decided it was better to prevent glare when you see leaving you no choice. With this G5, there is an AG coating, but it's acceptable if you want something as close to glossy as possible in this market today. Just please keep in mind, it's NOT a glossy display, it's just the least AG coated screen I've seen. Most TV panels are much better/closer to glossy (but not glossy,) this is not like that, this is like one step above a TV with a light AG coating, but let me be clear, if you ONLY want a glossy panel, this is not for you, you wont be happy with it at all, you'd look at this monitor as dull and lifeless and return it. What would be AWESOME is if Samsung made a glossy display like the S20 Ultra on their phone product line. I think the S20 Ultra was their last best glossy screen, would be awesome if they could make a monitor as glossy as that phone display. If it weren't such a pain to return the flat model and get a second one of these, I would do it in a heartbeat. The only thing I could see might be an issue for some people, is the stand on this model isn't adjustable almost at all. It is very stable, and if you plan to put it on a mounting arm it wont matter, but if you need to constantly adjust the angle of the monitor you might have an issue on some desks with this stand. However everything else is fantastic. If you are looking for a good budget monitor I can't recommend this one enough, even over other models in the same product line. If you are looking at the flat models, save yourself the disappointment and the $30 and go for this one instead.

review_title: Looks good in pictures and description. Return before 30 day window ends.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on May 12, 2026
review_body: Looks good in pictures but shows it flaws quickly. I love the Corsair brand and took a chance on this chair because it looks great. Some issues I found include: lumbar cushion is too large and impractical/uncomfortable; unusable. Head cushion is fine, but taller people will have to slouch for it to fit your neck and cause lower back pain; remove it and there is no neck support at all. back cushion material is very thin and will quickly give way to the lumbar frame, which is not comfortable at all. The entire chair mechanism and controls are cheap quality. Even in the locked position the chair still rocks back and forth to a small degree. You are constantly flexing your muscles just to stay in one because of the sway. The bolt holes are flimsy and even when tightened beyond capacity, the entire chair still rocks and flexes. No stability at all. Arm rests are completely fixed in place and can only go up and down. Arm rest surface is hard and uncomfortable. Arm rests stay in place when leaning back causing your arms to completely come off the arm rest or having to stretch both arms just to stay on the armrest, another huge inconvenience and ergonomic issue. Seat cushion is just thin as the back support. Thin cheap poly stuffing across metal frames. Get ready for serious lower back issues. Unless you are a small child, this chair is not for you. Now I know why they only give you 30 days to return the item. The chair shows its issues after that window closes.

review_title: Glad I bought it…Well not for long

I decided to just commit to it and order since I’ve always wanted this chair, and it matches my Corsair peripherals. I ordered it Monday, it came Wednesday, which is pretty awesome. Everything was well packaged. Branded bags, a lot of protection surrounding the products, I was impressed. It does NOT come with physical instructions, but you can just find them online. Super straight forward install which took me a solid half an hour at most. Now, the final verdict. First sit down and I was really impressed. The bottom cushion is honestly nice, and the two back pillows work well and fit my body like a glove. I’ve already used this for a consecutive couple of hours and I’m happier than I was in my other chair. I was rocking a Respawn 110 Pro, which is very large and plush but is very cheap feeling in comparison. For those looking to get this chair, every single one of the complaints I’ve seen did NOT fit my experience. Whether it be the parts, the bolts, the cushion, whatever. But I do understand where some of these may come from. Let me advise that this chair is absolutely perfect for me. Im 5’11 and 145 so I’m not your average bodybuilder. It still has some room but just be mindful of that since it does seem like it’s meant for the “smaller” peeps. Besides that, everything feels great and is premium. It left me surprised, and I will continue to not trust reviews and just get the dang thing myself. Glad I made the decision.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on December 15, 2019
review_body: I can't believe this coffeemaker is as highly reviewed as it is. First of all, the stainless steel carafe is impossible to pour because of the border at the top that goes in about an inch all the way around. When it's almost empty it is literally impossible to get the rest out without coffee spilling out the sides of the lid, so if you want to avoid spilling and wiping up every time the only option is to pour every cup over the sink, unless you're fine wasting half a cup of coffee every day, and even then you'll still need to pour it out before you brew the next pot. I know the reason for this is to keep the coffee hot, and this isn't unique to Cuisinart. All stainless steel carafes seem to have this design. review_body: I've used Keurig coffee makers for many years. I really like the K-Supreme. It's compact, brews a cup of coffee quickly, has a strong brew option and I like having the serving size options (4, 8, 10 and 12oz). The problem I had is it stopped working after 8 months - it would not power on. Granted I used the coffee maker a lot - 5 to 6 cups a day - but it should last longer than 8 months. My guess, and it's just a guess, is the thermal fuse went - there was a slight "burnt electronics" smell when it stopped working. Keurig did honor the 1 year warrantee and shipped me a brand new replacement unit at no cost and I did not have to return the defective unit. A word of warning, I had to prove the unit was purchased on Amazon and shipped directly by Amazon. Apparently, Keurig may not honor the warrantee if the unit was purchased from a third party seller. The warrantee claim process was challenging at best. The call center is most likely overseas. Information like your email address is repeated back to you in a Alpha Charlie Bravo manner. Even with that, the Agent got it wrong and I waited about a week for an email to start the claims process. A call back confirmand they had my email address wrong. I submitted the required proof of purchased information and my claim was denied. Another call resolved that when I pointed out the receipt showed I purchased the item on Amazon and I told the Agent I had additional proof the unit was shipped directly by Amazon. My claim was then approved and I received a brand new replacement with all accessories in about one week.

review_body: Meet cleavers are not just for cutting meat. I have had this knif for around a year. This is the best knife I have ever used for cutting ALL my food, not just meat. All the reviews that wrote that they can't get a sharp edge on it, don't know how to sharpen a knife! This is one of the easiest knives I've ever sharpened. I use a chefs rod sharpener and it come out very sharp EVERY time. If you don't know how to sharpen a knife, that is one thing. But don't write that it is a cheap knife that won't get a sharp edge just because you don't know how to sharpen a high quility carbon steel cleaver. And the review that said that it is to heavy, that he will be using it instead to chop wood, doesn't realize that all good quality cleavers are heavy like this. News flash. This is a meat cleaver. If you want a ax, go buy an ax. I have used it at least sixty times to cut food for dinner. This knife is made of fantastic high carbon stainless steel. It should be at least three times the price. That's how good this knife is. It also comes with a thick, good quality leather sheath. It is relitvly easy to sharpen. It really holds an edge incredably, once sharpened. The steel is not to hard where it becomes brittle. It's also not to soft where it won't hold an edge. The hardness is just the correct balance. It holds an edge better than my $150 great brand camping knife. Once the food is cut on my chopping block, I can easily scrap up the food onto the side of the knife, having the blade go under the side of my hand and pushing it onto the knife then picking up the food and putting it into a bowl, frying pan ect., just the way the chefs do in Chinese restaurants. It is much more efficient that way. That is what makes this a much better option for cutting ALL my food, rather than using a regular chefs knife. I know. I used to be a chef in a five star restaurant in CT. This knife is just as good as the expensive $140 knives that were bought from a restayrant supply company for the restaurant I worked at . So, buy it. You won't be disappointed with it!!!

review_title: ALL THE MONEY IN THE WORLD CAN'T BUY A BETTER COFFEEMAKER
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 13, 2026
review_body: With enough money in your bank account, you should be able to buy perfection in the form of a watch or a car or a purse that is damn near perfect. Not is the case with coffeemakers. I have spent weeks researching on Amazon and YouTube only to find out that each model at every price point falls short. It became very annoying to find that every machine I researched experienced one ore more of the following issues: settings too complicated to master, coffee takes too long to brew, coffee comes out of machine not that hot, coffee comes out of the machine bitter tasting, steam from machine smells like melting plastic, machine leaks while brewing, machine impossible to clean, carafe does not pour without spilling, machine stops working in a month and on and on and on. The more I researched coffee makers, the more pissed off I became. We have developed technology so that cars can drive themselves, but so many brands offer coffee makers incapable of doing what people have done manually for centuries. Even more interesting, those who bought more expensive machines wrote even more scathing reviews because their machines let them down equally. Reviews are important to me, and this coffee maker caught my attention because it has 4.6 STARS. It is not the most aesthetically pleasing small appliance in our kitchen, BUT it makes smooth, good tasting, hot coffee every morning. Coffee brews quickly and stays hot in the pot for hours. It is easy to figure out, simple to program, and easy to clean. I can't speak to reliability, but it seems to be well made and we've had no issues smelling burning or melting plastic while it's brewing. If it keeps working this well for the next couple months, I am going to buy a second one to keep in the closet just in case Kitchen Aid discontinues the one coffee maker on the market that actually works well. Super bowls have been won on the premise that true greatness comes from a relentless focus on and mastery of the simple, foundational elements of any task, making success an inevitable outcome of disciplined repetition. Why does this way of thinking has not been applied to design of coffee makers, I will never understand!!!

review_title: Those legs are ANNOYING to assemble, but otherwise decent chair
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on April 23, 2025
review_body: The hardest part about putting this thing together is the legs. It says "slap on floor" or something to get the screw holes to line up. THEY WON'T! What you really need to do is get it as close as possible to lining up, then put the bolt in at an angle but DO NOT SCREW IT IN! Put the tool into the bolt and then use the two to press inwards and kinda pry back the leg piece until the bolt stands upright like it should. THEN screw it in! A screwdriver won't work because it tends to slide right back out if you aren't holding it in place when you start to screw in the bolt. So when you remove the screwdriver to put the bolt in, you'll lose the alignment anyway. And you need the tool (included with it) in the bolt to be able to apply enough pressure while at an angle to "catch" the screw hole before pulling it into line.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on October 1, 2023
review_body: I bought this coffee maker after my previous one finally broke. I was specifically looking for a few key features which this coffee maker had. I wanted a coffee maker that had a mechanical On/Off switch, and I wanted a coffee maker that did NOT automatically shut off after a period of time. The reason I wanted these features is because I am slowly but surely turning my home into a “smart home” and I have been wanting to automate as many things as I can. Surprisingly at the time I was looking at this coffee maker I don’t believe there was a coffee maker with native Apple HomeKit compatibility. To my knowledge as of October, 2023 there still isn’t. That wasn’t a big deal, because I have a smart outlet that I plugged the coffee maker into. Now I can have the coffee maker turn on and start brewing coffee at whatever time I set up the automation for, so that when I finally get out of bed the coffee is already brewing. Yes, I could have done that with an automatic coffee maker that has a built-in timer, but this is great because I can program the outlet to turn on/off at various times or set up stipulations that someone has to be home in order for it work (preventing the coffee maker from doing its thing when we are away from home and forgot to turn off the auto feature on other coffee pots that we have had.)

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 5, 2018
review_body: So, like you all ,I've been a coffeeholic for many years. Like you ,I've struggled to have a decent maker in my kitchen. I recently finished up with my Cuisinart mod#CHW-12. Had it for 5yrs. It got to point of no longer producing a well tasting cup. We did the Vinigar cleaning etc. So, i spent MANY hours searching online for a decent Maker. Problem was the abundance of poor reviews encompassing many manufacturers! It's now 2018 and we have trouble creating a Kit Coffee Brewer thats decent! I did a switch and desired a maker that will produce a single cup as wife n i both have coffee at different times and mostly need the one 16oz cup. In searching for the 12cup Carafe / or single cup Maker ,my choices became limited. Read the reviews and pulled the trigger on this. It's only been 1wk now but i can honestly state that it is the BEST maker I've ever used! I ran a full 12cup Carafe first off, thn dumped. Then did same for the single cup side. ( full 14oz). Then ran 12cups clean water through for both. Then did the Coffee that I'll drink. No issues. Had to play round wth the exact amount of grounds for the single side so to get the outcome i desired. Has clock, easy to pre prog., and, the single side will turn off when done. The Carafe side will stay on (hot plate) for 2hrs after brewing complete. You can simply press On/Off button to turn off anytime. For those who have an over-spilling issue with the grounds within the gold filter basket?, you are using TOO MANY grounds! The single side comes with a gold reusable filter which also encompasses two - Level markers. One is min and the other is Max. If you fill above the Max level, WELL, overflow of grounds will prob. occur. On the Amazon site you'll see the Reusable filter for the Carafe side in " frequently ordered with". I also ordered that as i don't like paper filters. It performs well. Water level for Carafe is helpful. It's towards the right rear, on the side. It's accurate. Brew time for 12 cups was good. I've learned to warm up my Mug when using single side as it is not as hot as Carafe as no hot plate for the Mug. I use single side to run water for tea as well. What would make this model perfect? If it sounded out a tone when brewing is complete. It also has No charcoal filter as with my Cuisinart. No biggie as i always have used filtered water to begin with. Coffee is better when there's no Chlorine in the H2O! Filling either the Carafe or single side is easy and Max level markers are visible enough to get it right. Carafe pours very well and i like that the Carafe lid stays attached as u simply press thumb to open but it's not required to pour. Single side grounds chamber pulls out easily. Single side has a bottom (under mug/cup) that reverses to then become a elevator to bring cup higher if you'd like. I brewed a cup at lowest level without any spill or splatter. It drips slow enough that i don't believe i need to elevate my mug. This model also looks fantastic, Beautiful! Has a "Bold" brew mode for both Carafe n Sing. The brewing is slower, so u gt a richer brew. Light on clock only on when unit is ON. Has seperate green light that indicates you are using "Program" mode. I don't use "Pods" but if i did the manual states that "Senseo" Pods will work. Note that unit will only brew one side at a time. It cannot brew both sides at once. Very pleased so far. If any issues I'll update here. P.s. if Manufacturer reads this, you may want to consider modifying so to have an end of brew audible tone! Jst a thought. Update!; 1/5/18. Jst did 2 Lg mugs for me ( nine- 8oz cups), using Carafe of course. Wife then needed to do her single 14oz using of course the Single serv side. When throwing the slide switch over to Single, it turns off the Carafe side. So, yeah, hot plate under Carafe is still hot, but, it's now off. So, in future, wife does her single, first, then i do Carafe. UPDATE ; 1/22/18- 3wks now and NO ISSUES! When removing coffee filled Carafe, absolutely no spilling onto hot plate. The spring loaded valve above, performing well. Reviewers having the Hot plate discoloration or burning may be turning unit on with a Hot plate thats dirty. I make sure plate is clean /dry before and after ea. use. I make sure bottom of Carafe is clean/ dry as well. Wife using single serve ea. day and says " best cup of Coffee ever"! Update; 4/17/21. NO issues, all still good. UPDATE!!! - 10/10/21- So, finally I'm now considering buying a new one of these as this one is intermittently not pumping enough water up and into Coffee basket. About 12× now in past 6mon's I've had to pour out Carafe into another cup, place Carafe back, then pour my Coffee,(that looks like Tea), into the grinds basket and do a Double Drip, sometimes twice to get color I wish. I got roughly 3.5 years out of this Maker. I guess that's good considering Everything's made in Cheapo China. If/when I buy a new one, I'll post back. Have a good Coffee! UPDATE: 11/14/21. So, I purchased this exact model once again on 10/12/21. After 1 month, I can honestly state that it's a great difference between original and new. New machine brews perfectly as did the original one up until the 3yr mark. No issues to report with this New Maker( Same model as first one). Pictures here are of 2nd maker,(2021).

review_title: Very happy with this coffee maker!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on July 31, 2026
review_body: Delighted with this coffee maker! It arrived on time and in good condition. I had a very expensive coffee maker that quit working and thought I would save some money and try this Hamilton Beach version. SO glad I did!

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on June 30, 2026
review_body: It's about what you'd expect for a mid-range Hamilton Beach coffee maker. Normal price of $80 feels a bit steep, but I think it's worth what I paid for it on prime day. It does what it says on the box/product listing and it works better than the dollar store coffeemakers you'd find in an economy hotel room. Looks to be of quality from afar, is somewhat cheap and plastic feeling when you actually use it. Just sturdy enough that I'm not concerned that I'll break it. Single serve and full carafe functions do not share a water tank, and you fill the single serve reservoir with exactly as much water as you want to brew into coffee. Pretty intuitive and I guess pretty standard for this type of coffeemaker. But if you are used to filling the tank once a week and brewing a set 6oz or 8oz this is not that. "Brew Options" button toggles between bold and regular brew strength.... And that's it. There's no way to set brew temperature, but the default temperature is fine. It brews a single serve in about 3 minutes or so. Faster than a drip coffeemaker of yesteryear but if you're expecting it to be as fast as a pod system you're looking in the wrong place. The thing that matters most though is how the coffee comes out, and I have to say it's worth the extra hassle of using loose ground coffee and filters as it's much better than pod-brewed coffee. The slower brew speed results in a better coffee. Much more cost effective than pods too. The reusable single serve filter is surprisingly easy to rinse out. For $50 it's not bad. I would not pay $80 for this. At a price point of $80 I expect to at least be able to choose a brew temperature, even if there are a few pre-sets instead of by-degree. If you can get this for under $60 and you are specifically looking for a coffeemaker that doesn't use pods, then I can recommend it. Otherwise at full price, I don't think it offers enough to differentiate it from other $60 coffeemakers to justify the extra $20. It does have a clock in it and the ability to set a time to automatically start brewing at a set time, which is a feature I really don't use, but for some maybe this will make the $80 asking price worth it as I am not sure if this feature is commonly available in cheaper options.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on July 13, 2017
review_body: Just a short review, more of a user experience. I bought the D7500 for a month long trip to Europe. I was replacing a D7100 that had some nagging problems that often left me less than satisfied (It had been dropped - and repaired - early in its life, but was never as good as I expected). Anyway, I filled 4-5 64 Gig memory cards on the trip, and I have to say that this camera is far better than my old one. The low light abilities are awesome, and on the few instances where I needed to take a picture hand held in low light with some depth of field, ISO 16000 was a very viable option. Not noise free, but better than ISO 6400 on the older camera. Other features that made the user experience better: I could easily transfer pictures to my phone - very important to my wife and convenient for sharing or posting to Facebook when traveling without a computer. The connection to the phone also meant that I could share the phone's GPS with the camera and therefore get location tags on every photo. This worked very well, though it is possible that it negatively affects the phone's battery - but my phone is old and it is hard to really tell. (I think the automatic download was more detrimental to the phone battery, and it took a little searching to figure out how to turn off automatic downloads for every photo). As for the camera battery, it was also good, though again, the automatic download seemed to affect it a lot, as did a lot of activity on the display. The tilting screen was useful to have, but not as useful as a fully articulating screen (like the D5300). The touch screen was awesome, and made it VERY easy to check critical focus and work with the menu - even with gloves on. I was in a cold weather environment, so I had gloves on much of the time. These gloves had something on each finger that would let it work with an iPhone, and therefore it worked just as well with he camera. As a customer I should be able to buy something and get what I paid for, if such item doesn't work 100% out of the box I should be able to get a new one and not have it sent for repair (then what is their quallity control good for?) - I barely found any issues with the Nikon brand, I found more praises that anything else. The picture quallity is stunning, easy to use (I'm one that plays first then reads the manual) - colors are superv - the only thing I did not like is that it doesnt have "live view", meaning that you can't see on the screen what you are getting ready to shoot at, you have to use the viewfinder. It also has a feature that allows you to add filters after you have taken the picture, keeping the original intact. The viewfinder is very brigh and of good size. review_title: Wow! Very happy with this camera!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 23, 2019
review_body: I wanted to move up from my Canon Rebel t3 which I have been using since 2012. The high end Canons are beyond my budget. I stumbled upon this Canon 50D while I was browsing cameras here on Amazon. Yes it is discontinued by the manufacturer, yes it is older than my Rebel t3. The price was right so I thought I would take a chance on this camera. The listing described it as "very good". Excellent describes the condition of this camera more appropriately. I can find no scratch, smudge, ding, dent, wear and tear etc anywhere on this camera body. It came securely packaged and was delivered on time. In the box was the camera body, a battery and the battery charger. The charger and battery appear to be brand new also. The battery must have had a partial charge as it was fully charged within 20 minutes. A user's manual is not included with this package, but, having used the t3, I was able to make my way around it quite easily. I am told that manuals for all models can be downloaded from the Canon web site and I will eventually get the manual this way. I have a small collection of Canon, Sigma and Tamron lenses and they all work with this camera body. I live in NE Ohio and sun is a rarity here this time of year. I couldn't wait to try this camera out and, despite getting hit with winter storm "Harper" this weekend and being house-bound due to the weather, I decided to spend the time getting acquainted with this camera. These pictures (with the exception of the 2nd) were taken through a not so clean window at 3pm during the winter storm with gray light and falling snow. The camera seemed to focus quickly, shutter is fairly quiet compared to my t3. I used a Sigma 150-600mm sport lens with shutter speeds of 1/630 - 1/1250. My USB cord from my t3 worked just fine for this 50D . Pictures transfered effortlessly when I connected the 50D to my computer. Photos edited very slightly in Lightroom for crop and brightness. I mainly photograph birds/wildlife. Very happy with this camera and highly recommend this seller.

Also, it says you should unplug and thoroughly clean all parts of the coffee maker daily. That’s probably a good thing to do but I have only been cleaning mine periodically. review_date: Reviewed in the United States on October 12, 2020

The auto focus is very fast and it can continuously autofocus for example when your kid charges at you to see what picture you just took, you can just keep clicking. Our first trip was to the beach and I was blown away by the pictures. My T4i is a bit old at this point, but I didn't realize how old it was until i upgraded to the RP. Beaches have a lot of backlight reflected from the sand and water which causes people to appear as shadows. But even on auto, people's faces are bright, easy to see, and in focus and the background behind them isn't washed out. I had a much higher percentage of in focus, well balanced images to choose from than my old camera.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on November 13, 2025
review_body: My last coffee maker was the keurig duo. After 3 years it started making noises and brewing the wrong cup suzes. I searched every coffee maker for a replacement and found this ninja. I loved everything about it especially the ground coffee basket. It has an attached frother on one side and slide in basket on the other side which holds the ground coffee basket. The ground coffee scoop attaches to the side. It was packed in the ninja box in another. Everything was wrapped separately. It took a lot more time unpacking it than it did to set it up. I followed all the instructions step by step. It was actually quite easy. I flushed the water thru as instructed. Afterwards I put in a peets kcup hit go. It brewed the coffee which was surprisingly too hot to take more than a tiny sip. I really liked this machine and it came in moss green. I left for an hour. When i came back my counter was flooded with water. I immediately thought it was from my old keurig and i hadn't noticed it. I noticed to water tank only had a little bit of water in it. It still didn't click until i refilled the water reservoir and put it back on. Slowly water started seeping from underneath the machine. The water in the reservoir had bubbles. I immediately took the reservoir off and put it on a dry paper towel to look for a crack. There wasn't one and the water wasn't bubbling off the machine. The water was still coming from under the machine because it was already in there. I thought check with Amazon online. I put in the info and the reply was i can get a refund. I didn't want a refund i wanted to exchange it. Nope have to return to kolhs not whole foods or Amazon fresh right below me. I decided to check the instruction sheet again. Ah troubleshooting. There's a section on leaks. The very last scenario is if leak is coming from under the machine call customer service. I call and was pleasantly surprice how easy it was to get to talk to a person. Kellie was very personable. I explained the leaking from under the machine. The impression i got from her was this isn't a common problem we did a video chat she looked at the machine i showed her where the water was coming from. There are 2 empty holes on the bottom. I showed her i can stick my pen up into them. The other holes like those have a screw in them. There are also non skid dots on the corners. She had me put the reservoir with water back on. It took maybe 30 seconds and i said bubblesare starting to form which she was able to see. Luckily i had the dry paper towel where it was as the water began seeping out for her to see in real-time. I told her i thought it was coming thru the holes i could stick my pen into. I was on the phone with her for 30 minutes. Yes they would send me a new machine but even if i cut off the cord the needed this one back. They won't pick it up. I would have to take it the FedEx. There isn't a FedEx anywhere near me. There are a few UPS but it can't go there. They can't send the new until they get they get the defective one. It would a few weeks to get the new one. I thought shark/ ninja would want to look over the machine to find the defect. Then i thought why did i bother and go thru all of this when i can return it to amazon and reorder it. I wasted at least 30 minutes on the phone with shark ninja and didn't get anywhere while water was still leaking from under machine. I thought i was a doing a good thing in case other people were having the same problem. After reading many of the good reviews i decided to read the bad. I'm not the only one with a leaking machine. I packed everything up and put the machine and all parts back into the box to return to amazon. I was going to reorder one even tho they were out of the green before i got to return this one. In 2 or 3 days the price went way up. Now they have 3 different models of this machine. The one i had with the frother was 99.00. I think it's now 30.00. I can do without the frother i only cared about the ground coffee basket. I've been using my french press because i don't have a machine. I'm debating if i should order the one without the frother or buy a new keurig that comes with a basket for grounds.

It is so quiet! It will make a variety of sizes for ups, mugs, travel mugs, and iced coffee. One of the features I look for is the ability to brew a strong cup from a pod. The “rich” function on this machine, does the trick! It doesn’t just run water straight through the pod, so that the flavor is lacking. It puts water through the pod in increments to get as much flavor as possible. I used the “over ice” function for the first time yesterday, and it also works slowly enough to pull as much flavor as it can. It was delicious! The brew time is really short, and yet the coffee tastes wonderful, and the temperature is perfectly hot. The machine and it’s components are very easy to clean. It takes up more space from front to back, but has very slim lines and looks good on the counter. The water tank is easy to remove, clean, and fill. I know a couple of people have mentioned having an issue with “exploding pods.” I had this happen ONE time, but I immediately realized why. When you put the pod in the machine, if you just pull the lid down, it may not fully puncture the bottom of the pod appropriately. This causes the hot water to overfill the pod, and it bursts from the pressure. There is a super simple fix!! All you have to do is place the pod in the machine, and press it down, so you feel it puncture the bottom of the pod. THEN close the lid to puncture the top! That’s it! Nothing difficult or time consuming. Just press the pod down before you close the lid. Problem solved! I haven’t had any issues since! 😊 I really am enjoying the ease of use and versatility of this machine. I think it is well made, and will be used for a long time. It is sturdy, without being bulky or heavy. The materials are sleek and easy to clean. I looked at dozens of coffee makers, and read SO many reviews before I made this purchase. The comments about the potential “exploding pods” had me a little concerned, but as I said, that won’t ever be a problem for me after realizing what can cause the issue. I’m an extremely picky person when it comes to my beloved coffee maker, and this Ninja has won me over!

review_body: This is by far the best quality espresso machine at a reasonable price point for your home. My ex husband's father bought us this machine in 2012 and it works perfectly still in 2026. I bought my own machine recently because my ex husband kept our first machine when he moved out. My new version of the same Breville Barista Express is just as awesome and easy to set up and get started as the old machine was. Much to my excitement, I guessed correctly on my first try with the grind size and grind amount. I brewed the perfect espresso with an amazing crema head. I was historically a barista while in college, and this tiny little inexpensive machine makes espressos and lattes just as well as any Starbucks barista can. I waited until this machine went on sale for $500 on Christmas Day and bought it. It also goes to that price on Black Friday or cyber monday. Fun fact, it was $500 in 2012, so it has not increased in price when you wait for the sale price. When you think about how much you would spend at Starbucks everyday, this machine pays for itself in less than 6 months. I'm a huge fan of the hot water feature, as I love to make Americanos. In case anyone wants to know, I use the brand of coffee called Purity, and love the "Ease" flavor. The beans work so well with this machine. I also highly recommend buying the Breville knock box for your grind bricks. This particular machine also comes with something that the old one did not, which is a spill proof topper for when you are grinding. It clicks right on and prevents you from spilling precious ground coffee, but has a wide mouth for easily tamping all of the grounds down before you remove it and brew the espresso. I just love this machine. If you do like lattes, the frother works so well with any type of milk. I have used almond milk, soy milk, and regular cow's milk. It's easy to clean if you immediately wipe it down with a wet paper towel. I can't say enough awesome things about it. There are so many others like this machine, but this one is the best.

review_body: This is the first espresso machine I've ever owned. I purchased it this Spring (2020) because, like many of you, I needed to stop going out. I didn't know much about home brewing espresso, but I have lots of Breville products, and I thought this would be a good entry-level machine., I liked that it had all of the features I needed in a one-stop solution, but would still allow me to make "real" espresso, not the stuff that shoots of a pod, which I typically dislike. Armed with nothing more than the instructions it came with, power, water, and beans, I was able to brew espresso good enough to keep me from going into withdrawal, but typically not delicious, and appreciably less enjoyable than my favorite baristas in my favorite cafes. I also wasted a lot of beans in the process. After about 10 days of this bumbling around, I decided to start researching how to get better performance, learning a lot of coffee science along the way, and over the next few months, my technique and results improved, but ultimately plateaued at a point where I felt my home-brewed espresso was now generally better than my favorite baristas - but still not consistent - one day I could make a perfect shot, with all of the lovely sweetness and velvety texture of great espresso, with little or no extraction defect, but then the next day, doing the exact same thing, would get something uneven and over- or under- extracted, and not as good. I was not exactly sure what the variable was, but I suspected it was the grind consistency, since by now I had become very practiced at everything else.

I read several reviews prior to purchase that claimed the temperature of the brew was not as hot as was set in the machine. I experienced the same and wanted to understand it better. I have my machine set at 190 for the temperature. I used a calibrated Thermapen ONE Thermometer, the one chefs use and rely on, and the temp of the coffee in my cup right after brewing completed was 158. Then I measured the brew as it exits the machine but before it got into my cup and it was 187. Turns out my ceramic cup was at room temperature and some of the heat from the brew was used up to heat my cup, which lowered the resultant temp of the coffee in my cup. Bottom line: my machine is very close to the temp I set for the brew. If I preheat my cup the coffee in my cup will be very close to what I have my machine set to. So I am happy and my coffee maker is performing as specified.
