review_body: This camera is terrible in every aspect and design, to get the SD card out you have to open the battery compartment, which when doing so you loose all the settings as in date and time on the camera and you have to completely reset everything. If you use the cord to download the pictures to your computer instead of taking out the card it drains the batteries very quickly. Even when not using the cord to download, the batteries drain very quickly, it's such an issue that it's one of the trouble shooting things that they have listed with this camera. There solution is to shut off any apps or things on the camera you're not using, tells you to turn down the brightness of the screen. Really your solution to this problem is to disable features that are on this camera, what's the point of having those features if when using them they drain the batteries very quickly. Let me explain what I use this camera for, to take pictures of items I sell on line. I put in a new set of energizer batteries, tested them with my ohm/volt tester, they tested 1.58 volts. I took 17 pictures downloaded them by using the cord and then I took 10 more pictures and the camera shut off and right before it did it said batteries expired. So I took the batteries out and tested them and they tested 1.28 volts, which will make most things still run, like my game cameras. There's definitely an issue with these cameras and the power they use and how fast they drain batteries. I've also have had it lock up and stop working several times and it wouldn't shut off or do anything, had to open up the battery compartment which takes all the power from the camera so it will reset and then close it and then turn it back on. I had a Sony Cyber shot which they don't make anymore, for over 10 years and I took literally thousands of pictures with it and it cost half as much and the pictures were clearer and of higher quality than what this camera is capable of taking. I would still be using the Sony, but some how it developed a gray spot that was showing up in all of my pictures and it was causing potential buyers to ask what that spot was on the item. So I had to stop using it and bought this camera thinking it would work great for what I was doing and also work great for taking pictures of nature and wildlife. I wish I would have sent it back right away, but I figured I would give it a chance to get better, because they said it would if I did the update. But just for a good consistent pot of coffee once you get the correct measurements of coffee and water I think there is none better. It came with the gold filter which is good since I never use paper, it has a few brew temp and carafe temps and you can set the timer to brew automatically. It does not take up much space is fairly easy to keep clean. The water tank though does take a bit of work to get clean and keep clean though. Over time it gets pretty rank and I cleaned mine by spraying soap and Clorox in it and using a dishrag to clean it out. I then rinsed it out in the sink all the time being upside down so as this would not enter the brew track. Once cleaned and rinsed then filled with water and ran a couple of pots of water through it and its as good as new. Now unless your a professional, I don't recommend doing this LOL but it never stopped working and never stopped brewing a good cup of coffee. Looks and works as good as the day it was purchased. review_body: Ordered this for my wife to take pictures of birds in our yard using a lens hood and UV filter (both must be purchased separately). It has not been used indoors. The major problem with this camera is the lack of a viewfinder. Pictures must be set up using the small LCD screen on the back of the camera. Unfortunately, when you use the camera outside, the screen shows your own reflection looking back at you and you can't see what you are aiming at. I contacted Kodak customer service to see if anything could be done about this: perhaps a non-reflective coating that could be applied to the screen. This was their reply: "...when hit with sunlight the screen will look black and the only thing you can do is hover your hand over the top of the camera to keep the sun from hitting the LCD screen before pressing the shutter button." Unless you have 3 hands or are using a tripod this is an unworkable solution. The shutter and zoom controls are on the right side of the camera so you hold the camera on the right. You need to steady the camera with your left hand when the zoom is extended because the camera becomes front heavy. Using this camera is like standing in a crowd and holding your cell phone over your head to try to take a picture of something you can't really see. Sometimes you get a good picture, most times you don't. It's not point and shoot - it's guess and hope.

The fact it comes with 8 brush heads, a little traveling case and 2 tooth brush head protectors is value in itself. Now, I liked how the toothbrush head clicks and locks into place, so you know it's not going to fall off. The handle is fairly easy to hold but nothing spectacular about that. The motor and the handle portion feel a bit cheap, again going back to the quality of the brush heads being the best part, this part doesn't live up to the remainder of the brush. Additionally all the heads and the extras you get are great, BUT to charge you have to use the supplied charger, why not a universal type USB-C that everyone is using nowadays. Secondly I feel slightly uncomfortable that the charging port does not have a cap on it, so the toothbrush handle ends with a flat, blunt edge where you use the adapter to charge. And if you're like me, I brush my teeth in the shower in the morning, so I know it's being exposed to water and toothpaste ECT. That is the only reason for the 4 stars and not 5. -No universal charger port, no cover to the charging port and handle is fairly inexpensive feeling, however it is a good toothBRUSH and for the price you pay it is worth the investment. I feel if they fix those few things they'd be right up there with Phillips and other well known toothbrush makers. 4 out of 5 with potential to be a solid 5 with some fine tooning.

review_title: Definitely in the "You Can't Go Wrong With It" category.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 13, 2026
review_body: Great speaker. I have tried several brands of these bt speakers; Tribit, Soundcore, Harmon Kardon, Bose, B&O and a few others. None compare to this for the qualities I want in a bluetooth speaker. I see it as a personal speaker for listening to music privately and for podcasts. I have a nice stereo system for serious listening, but it's not always convenient to do that. What I found was that there is a lot of sound profile manipulation by the producers of these products favoring bass output, because that's what a large portion of the buying public thinks is "good sound", with the resulting side effects on the rest of the profile.. The Wonderboom might tweak it a little, but not even close to overdone. The sound quality is really solid, including the mids and trebles. Clear and full; undistorted. Bass is solid, but balanced. Clearly present but not obnoxious. That's number one. It is light, and it is the easiest to use of the bunch. The 360 degree sound is a real plus and does fill the room. It is well protected against dust and moisture, and it floats if you drop it in the lake. It is very nicely shaped, easy to pick up, hold, carry , pack. Use it anywhere. It also has zero over compensating frills, like apps and equalizers, which are a total waste of time on something that you just want to work and not have to fuss over. This one does just that, and it has better sound quality than all the others tested, except the Luna 2 and B&O a1, but, at lower volumes it is pretty much indistinguishible.. I've sent one to my son and one to my daughter, who took it to the lake house last weekend and said it was a real hit on the dock and the boat with over a dozen people in the group, whom she said were universally complimentary. It does have two adjustments. The basic mode is "standard'. Push the button once and it gives you an "outdoor boost"; again and you get "podcast mode", which I found not to be necessary, but it does help if there is ambient noise, like, say, a shower. I also tried it in stereo with another unit and it's great. I don't really need that function, but I just might hang onto the second one and do the stereo anyway. These these little guys are affordable enough that you can get two for less than a competitive single unit will cost and you can bet that they'll sound better. Great product. Well conceived, well designed and well executed. A truly great product.

review_title: Better than Phillips Sonicare. App is actually useful and not just a gimmick.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on October 2, 2023
review_body: So, I'm a long-time user of Sonicare, which means I've gone through a number of them that always tend to break right at warranty expiry. Though I usually find them on sale, they are not cheap, nor are the brushes, and for the price they are still so prone to breaking down and various issues. So, when my current one started to have an issue (turning on randomly on its own, startling all around), I started shopping for a replacement. This Oral B brush went on sale, so I decided to check it out - maybe return if it wasn't all that great in comparison. At first, I was a little confused, because I thought these brushes mainly worked by rotation, but they are both that and sonication. I don't know if the vibration speed matches to Sonicare, but it doesn't seem critical. One immediate thing I noticed was the light ring which instantly lets you know if you are pressing too hard or not enough. As somebody with gum issues, this is appreciated. Next thing, do set up and try out the app. I was skeptical, but it really does a good job of figuring out what part of your mouth you are brushing, apparently by some kind of bluetooth-based sonar and something in the brush that can tell if it's facing up or down. It's not to the level of knowing which tooth, but it maps the front and two sides of both the top and bottom of your mouth, which is still pretty detailed. Rather than just using some kind of timer, it tracks that you spend the proper amount of time in each of the 6 regions. Your coverage within each region is then up to you. Sure, there are some times when it is a bit off, but I find that that tends to happen if I turn my head. So if you keep your head still, it seems to work more accurately. Not too hard to do. Besides the main brush tracking, you can set specific goals, and it will add recommendations for other steps like tongue brushing and flossing. I started a program for plaque removal. So now, instead of brushing or not kind of mindlessly in the shower one a day, I have started brushing twice a day, with more intention, and it's even slightly fun. And so far, my teeth feel smoother and cleaner. I also get less gum bleed, perhaps due to avoiding pressing too hard. I think this is still a bit pricey at full price, but maybe in this case it could be worth it for the improvement in your teeth and gum health. On sale, I can definitely recommend. Will it last long term? We'll see.

I brush longer and use the guided brushing to make sure I'm getting full coverage. The only thing is that the zone identification is sketchy. On almost every brushing, it indicates the wrong active area of my teeth. I've tried Oral-B's recommendations- stand straight, do each tooth one at a time, move to different segments, repeat on inside and bite surfaces- but it still misdetects zones. What that does is make me brush even longer, so not terrible, but better accuracy would be much better and, frankly, I expected much better. Occasional it totally glitches and I need to restart the app and the brush. I also thought the battery would lastonger but it's about the same as my OG Oral-B electric that was around $40. Note that I am probably brushing longer, so maybe the battery is a little better but I hoped for 3 weeks and I'm getting less than 2 between charges. I still like the brush, but just know the app guidance doesn't work as well as you'd think. I do like that it reminds you to floss, brush your tongue, and use a mouth rinse. It also gives you a score for each session and a running score, which I like even though I thought I'd never use that. In summary, it works well and my dentist noticed a difference and told me to keep it up. It is a bit expensive for an electric toothbrush, so I hope it lasts a long time.

review_body: È piccolo, perciò non ci si può aspettare miracoli, ma se vengono rispettate le indicazioni del produttore utilizzandolo in stanze delle adeguate dimensioni, lavora benissimo, e purifica l'aria correttamente. Tutto sembra essere costruito con ottima qualità: plastiche, incastri, motore ventola ecc... Perfino il filtro sembra essere ben costruito e di qualità superiore rispetto ad altri della stessa fascia di prezzo. Ha una regolazione di 3 velocità delle quali solo la massima è rumorosa ma non molto fastidiosa, infatti la velocità intermedia è appena udibile (pari ad un soffio) e mai fastidiosa anche stando nelle vicinanze. Alla prima velocità è praticamente impossibile udire qualcosa e questo è un pregio ENORME rispetto ad altri purificatori in commercio della stessa categoria. Questa velocità si presta benissimo per il riposo notturno. Nessun ronzio o rumore. Questo, forse, credo sia possibile anche grazie al motore/ventola in corrente continua, infatti il purificatore viene fornito di un piccolo alimentatore che si trova nella confezione. In essa vengono forniti anche 3 "feltri" per la diffusione delle essenze naturali da inserire in un apposito cassetto laterale quasi invisibile. Nel complesso quindi un ottimo purificatore poco ingombrante, con un buon rapporto qualità prezzo e soprattutto poco rumoroso e che vale la pena acquistare.

review_title: A really great air purifier that has many key improvements/advantages over its competitors
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on May 12, 2026
review_body: I got this air purifier for a relative that has COPD. They already had an Alen T100 that they were pleased with. But, as is common in multiple industries where a core product requires a consumable, it's often not the condition of the core product but the availability of the required consumable that dictates when a product has to be replaced. While I've been able to find enough replacement air filters for that one air purifier, when the need arose for a 2nd air purifier for a second section of the house, instead of just getting a newer Alen, I opted to start the research process all over again and, this time, the clear winner was Coway And, as well as the Alen has done over the years, it didn't take long to see how much better the Coway model was by comparison. A first major difference is in the design and aesthetics. With several color variants and another model with a more classic look, it doesn't visually stand out as much as a typical tower air purifier does. It's more stylish and "elegant". Second, there are actual very practical functional reasons for those aesthetics. Instead of blowing air on people horizontally, it blows the air straight up so that nobody feels the air blowing. It's also significantly quieter so even set on medium speed it's quieter than the Alen at low speed. That's impressive given that this model is designed to handle a space 3X as much as the Alen was. But, it's due to the design of having the air come in from the sides and then exit out the top. It just provides a much more natural method of air circulation. And, also means it can be tucked along a wall and out of the way ... with the cord blocked from view if located directly at the power outlet. Another great feature that the Coway has that I haven't seen before is that you have 4 stage filtration .... with the initial pre-screen stage being a built-in filter that can be washed ... followed by the 1st charcoal filter to catch large objects like hair .... followed by a 2nd filter that have 4 replacement options and therefore can be customized based on what types of odors or particles a person needs filtered out ... and finally the HEPA filter that catches the smallest particles that make it past the other three. Not only is this like a coin-sorter process of filtering out different things at different people ... but this is why, unlike a lot of air purifiers, the main filters can last 1 year instead of just 6 months. The built-in filter is recommended to be cleaned once a month. The charcoal filter 6 months. The "environmental/smell" filter being replaced once a year. And, the HEPA filter being able to last even longer depending on environment. Where it actually gets better at filtering over time ... but then the tradeoff is air flow reduction. That's why the official recommendation is still once a year. And, best of all, the NYT wirecutter review I'd found says Coway has made continual improvements over the years to this product, which really shows. Many manufacturer's just seem intent on constantly reinventing the wheel and it seems Coway was instead focusing on perfecting what it already had. Very pleased with the results and the good deal we'd gotten on it. While we hope the Alen continues to do well for several more years, at least it's nice knowing that we already know what to replace it with whenever it become necessary.

review_title: Super clean air purifier with unique features
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 10, 2026
review_body: A really good air purifier with some unique features. In terms of noise, it is among the quietest at about 60 DB. Obviously there’s more noise the faster the fan spins, but in automatic mode, it senses the amount of gluten in the air and adjust the speed automatically which means most of the time it will be running at low speed unless there’s a lot of dust in the air. You can download an android or iOS app to control the fan speed and to see how much dust it is seeing in the air. You can also set it up for Alexa or Google Home to be able to control it through those devices. One need feature is being able to ask Alexa for a reading of air quality from the device. You can also enable an automatic sleep mode, which basically keeps the device on auto fan mode where it senses the amount of dust in the air during daylight, but when the device notices that the room is dark at night, it will put the fan speed to its slowest mode to ensure that there’s minimal noise during nighttime hours. Once the room is lit again and it is daylight the device will automatically switch to auto mode and if necessary, increase the fan speed to pull in more air if it detects an increased amount of dust. These are the main features of the device, but the other thing that I liked about it compared to similar models from other brands is that they say the standard filters it comes with should last 12 months where many other brands recommend changing filters after three months. This is probably because the HEPA filter that this device comes with is thicker at about 1 inch compared to what I have on other air purifiers filters that are generally 1/2 inch or less thick. I have not yet replaced my filters, but with an estimate of one year it should not be a substantial yearly cost because filter filters run around $20. And I say filters because as you can see in the images for the product, there are actually two separate filters that work together one is a white HEPA filter to filter out particles. The other one is a black carbon filter, which filter filters out smell smells. And holding both of those filters in place is a screen which is washable that is meant to capture, larger dust particles or pet hair before they hit the main filter filters. Overall, very satisfied with this device and the only thing I can’t really comment on is how long it will last as I’ve only recently started using it.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on March 31, 2020
review_body: I only just got this yesterday and used it last night for the first time but I feel compelled to write a quick review already. This thing is a game. changer. Ever since moving to Texas, I suffer from terrible seasonal allergies. I never have in my life until now (turns out I'm allergic to a handful of trees that are native around here. Fun.) Some years are worse than others but this year is baaad. For the past few weeks my mornings have had me waking up congested and unable to breathe, blowing wads of snot out of my nose (sorry!), and with a itchy/scratchy sore throat. First thing I do is take an allergy pill and wait in misery until it finally seems to kick in around mid morning. (I've had a terrible time finding meds that work too. It just sucks.) I don't know why I never thought to get an air purifier. I guess when I thought of air purifiers I'd always think of the fancy Dyson ones that cost hundreds of dollars. I mean, puh-lease. Not happening. Then I found this little guy. Had great reviews, was the perfect little size for our master bedroom (216sqft), and reasonably priced with reasonably priced replacement filters. In a plee of desperation I talked my husband into us trying it. It got in yesterday (quicker than expected, yay!). I immediately unboxed it upon getting home from work and plugged it in. It says you only need to run it for about 15-20 minutes on high to cycle the room but I set that little baby on high with a two hour timer and let it run. When it was time for bed, I set the 6 hour timer on sleep mode. The sleep mode is great. It's a lot more quiet than I expected. I still expected to be able to hear a little white noise from it (which doesn't bother me at all) but unless I lift my head off the pillow and really listen, I can only just baaarely hear it. And I have it on my side of the bed about 3 feet away. Our home air system is louder than it on sleep mode. If you enjoy white noise, you could probably just run it on low and be fine. It has a button to turn off the indicator lights at night too so you don't have bright lights keeping you awake if that's a problem for you. Anyway, I woke up this morning with NO allergy symptoms. None. No congestion, absolutely clear nasal passages, and NO sore throat at all! I'm blown away. I'll try to come back and revise this review if my opinion changes but after the first night and the relief I was FINALLY able to feel from my allergies this morning I absolutely rate this thing 5 stars. Worth every penny!

review_title: Cost effective for small spaces/limited use

review_body: An air purifier is not a complicated device. It is a fan, and an air filter. The fan pulls air through the air filter, and catches various particles and impurities in the air. As long as you have a decent HEPA filter, and a fan that has enough velocity to circulate the room air through the filter effectively, it will work to clean the air. You can build one yourself with a box fan and some high quality furnace filters and duct tape if you have to.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 7, 2026
review_body: Impressive. It is whisper quiet, and extremely effective. I’ve been sick all week from the wildfire smoke in the Denver area. I happened to be talking to a friend on the phone when I received my LEVOIT air purifier. I set it up while we chatted and within half an hour I could tell that the air quality had improved. I was breathing easier and my friend said she could hear it in my voice - it wasn’t as rough and nasally. It says it is for a room up to 222 square feet, but it is portable (under 10 lbs), about the size of a wastebasket, it plugs in to a regular outlet, and I can physically only be in one room at a time. It cleared the air so quickly that I can probably manage with just the one for the rest of the wildfire season. But it was very cost-effective, under $100, so I may go ahead and get another one for the kitchen next week. (I am a senior on a fixed income, but this is a necessity if I want to be able to breathe in my own house when the air quality outside is so bad.)

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on June 12, 2026
review_body: We have 2 in our house and looking to purchase a 3rd. Love these things! Ours run all the time and after a couple of years are still going strong! I can't attest to any personal allergy relief since my immediate family doesn't really suffer from much (maybe due to the purifiers) but I do feel a peace of mind having them in our home, especially with pets! Does a great job to trap dust and debris. I am always very surprised to find how much these things pick up when I check/change the filter. I also appreciate the white noise that it gives off. We do run ours on the 3 setting most days and it provides a nice background noise, which is a personal preference for my family. There are 2 other lower settings which are much much quieter. The purifier is easy to use and easy to maintain (filters can be a pricey). I will actually clean the filter a few times before purchasing new and have found that works great for us and saves an extra buck. We have two white ones and find that they look nice and blend in well with the rooms they are placed in. One of the purifiers is in a space between the living room and kitchen area (most traffic and use) and the other is near our home office and entry. I feel that they do a good job for the space size. Would definitely recommend!

review_title: Levoit Air Purifier Home Allergies, Asthma
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 8, 2026
review_body: I love the Levoit Air Purifier! It is very quiet all of the time, but if you use the night time sleep mode, you can just barely hear it at all. The fan has three speeds as well as the sleep mode. You can set the sleep mode for up to 8 hours, the best I remember. I do use sleep mode but not with the timer. You can turn off the display panel and I do that at night because I prefer a totally dark room. I run it all day on low and so far, a week out from getting it and setting it up, there are no signs of anything that needs to be cleaned from the outside as I've seen in other reviews. I don't have any pets, just nasty carpet. I call it nasty, because all carpet is nasty to me. I dislike carpet so much! I don't have a choice, though. I think the filter is supposed to last around six months, so we shall see. I bought a replacement filter when I bought the purifier and several filters for the humidifier, as well. It looks like I may have to change the Humidifier filter once a week as a week out, it is starting to turn brownish-yellow around the top of it. I don't smoke and do try to keep an extremely clean place, so not sure what the discoloration is. I'm the only one who has ever lived here. I use distilled water but also bought the demineralization kit and extra filters for the humidifier in case I run out of distilled water and have to use tap water. I clean the humidifier every day. It's not hard to do once you do it. I love the modern look and it is built very well. It's really not hard to use at all. I believe it is super effective combined with my also Levoit Humidifier. I have them on opposite sides of my small bedroom as I couldn't put my humidifier under the smoke alarm. My skin feels much softer and cleaner using the both of them. I could instantly tell a difference in how well I could breathe using the them. As before purchasing them, I couldn't breathe out of my nose at all. The humidity is brutal here. I have been able to get the humidity down to 58, which is something the local meteorologist said couldn't happen in these heatwave temperatures! Ha! I only use GENUINE LEVOIT filters and they're a bit more costly, but I prefer to use the real deal and have less problems/headaches. It can be a bit catchy to find them on Amazon and the generic ones keep popping up; however, I went straight to the Levoit store to get the genuine ones. Blessed to be able to somewhat better control my Asthma and all-season Allergies with the help of these two awesome products! Thank you, Amazon and Levoit! Sorry for combining reviews but I need to do a copy and paste for the humidifier as it will save me time doing it this way.

review_title: A versatile, compact charger for your car battery
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on July 30, 2026
review_body: The NOCO Genius 5 is a very compact device that does a great job charging my car battery. There's no digital readout but it's easy to read that the battery is more than 25%, 50%, or 75% charged, and over time, 80%-90% charged and in trickle mode. At full charge the lights will indicate 100%. It's very easy to use. Select your battery type and attach the positive clamp to the positive battery terminal. Ideally you then connect the negative clamp to the car frame or a metal bracket for ground. In my case, though, doing so didn't work. The NOCO would not recognize and read the battery. That can happen when the parts you've grounded to are painted or coated, so the fix was to attach the negative clamp to the negative battery terminal. After doing so the charge worked fine. There's built-in intelligence so it's hard to screw up. You can't overcharge because the battery in trickle mode won't let you do so, and if you leave it connected long-term, it will continue to charge as needed to keep a full charge, but won't do any damage by overcharging. If you choose the wrong battery type, apparently it will know that too and it won't start charging at all. Also, btw, if you have a car battery that's fully discharged and therefore not visible to the NOCO, you can put the charger into a "forced mode" to start charging. All pretty impressive features and, when you need it, it's a great device to own. Two final comments: the charger does not come with a carrying case but there are various options online that are sized to this particular model. I will post a separate review of the one I purchased. Lastly, I did have an issue with the first charger I received. It just would not recognize my car battery. My request to return it was quickly authorized and the replacement unit I purchased later on worked totally fine.

review_date: Reviewed in Mexico on August 26, 2022
review_body: El cargador llego en un día, el precio en Amazon esta elevado comparado con otros sitios sin embargo la recepción en un día me favoreció. Me lo recomendó un amigo que se dedica a la mecánica automotriz, mi camioneta apenas encendía, especialmente los lunes después de no usarla sábados y domingos, las primeras dos fotografías muestran el estado del acumulador (LTH AGM 48, 760CCA y 70AH) antes de usar el NOCO Genius10, básicamente parecía que el acumulador estaba bien cargado sin embargo se bajaba rápido y le faltaba potencia de arranque, después de conectarlo al Genius10 y dejar que realizara una carga completa (aproximadamente unas 4 horas y hasta que el led verde dejo de parpadear), para después correr el reparador por aproximadamente 4 horas más la batería quedo completamente restaurada, como se puede ver en las dos siguientes fotografías. Ya instalado de regreso en mi camioneta el arranque es inmediato y sin esfuerzo. La batería ya se había cargado antes con otros cargadores diferentes, pero no funcionaba bien casi de inmediato daba problemas en el arranque de nuevo y el SOH (state of health) seguía en los 80,s ahora es del 100%, así mismo el estado de carga (SOC) nunca llegaba al 100%... este cargado rehabilito mi acumulador con alrededor de dos años de uso, y que por descuidos míos se había dejado descargar al dejar accesorios prendidos en la camioneta en varias ocasiones. Lo recomiendo ampliamente.

review_body: So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on April 30, 2026
review_body: Ok so I purchased this Garmin 165 watch for just $200. So the price was excellent. It has a nice bright amoled screen and has a good build quality. However, I only use this watch as a fitness, wellness and running watch. That is, I turned off the notifications. I don't see the point of trying to read a notification or message on a watch face when my phone is right next to me. So with notifications turned off I got 13 days of battery life before the watch went down to 9%. I also do not have on the "always on display". With this set up you can get 13 days of regular (non smart watch) use. This is what I wanted the most, a descent battery. So having to just charge the watch every 2 weeks or twice a month is really great. I also wore the watch every day and did walking workouts. One thing to note : I DID NOT SLEEP WITH THE WAATCH ON... I do not know if that helped the battery life but I generally do not sleep with any watched or rings or anything restrictive when I sleep.. I need comfort... lol.. But I did sleep one night with it and it was comfortable.. just not my thing... but great watch, connected to GPS is seconds, gives good info in the app and is comfortable. Highly recommend for someone who is into fitness... it can track most activities like running, walking, swimming, hiking, trail run, in door run etc.. most general activities.... look... there is really no need to go out an buy a $500 or $900 watch.. this one does the job at $200.. no point getting a watch that gives you tons of stats that you will not use or understand... if you do triathlons or want those pretty maps on the watch then by all means get the more expensive watch but if you just want to keep healthy and run.. then this watch is prefect..

The sleep metrics are detailed well, I just wish the alarms were louder. The set up was very easy to complete, just create a Garmin account, sync your watch, and boom, you’re in. The battery life is insane, up to a week of battery for me (depending on usage) and very fast to charge. I like that the bands are removable to make it easier to clean the watch after getting sweaty or dirty. The watch itself is clean looking, I love the black color with the grey band.

review_title: Budget HE keyboard that gives you all you need...
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 12, 2025
review_body: AULA WIN68 HE is my first ever HE keyboard, after years of being in the world of mechanical keyboards and exclusively favoring the brown switch (tactile) I always watched many videos and people praising HE keyboards and the edge they give to you in gaming primarily. We all know of the famed Wooting 60 HE which started this trend in gaming world both the price and being only 60% give's it only a small and competitive market for a few individuals that can afford it or need it for professional e-Sports. As primarily a single-player gamer I was blow away with how much HE switches changes your experience of playing and gives you for the first time ever something that gamepads had over keyboards, and that is you don't need to push the key all the way for it work, both only a slight push fulfils the given command that you want (MMOs and racing games benefit from this the most). The web software is one of the best features of this keyboard and it allows you to customize every single key however you want it, every key supports rapid trigger as well as customizing the dead zone as well as primarily the sensitivity of the keys. The standard version that I have allows you to customize the sensitivity from 0.8mm to larger if you prefer (default being 1.70mm, while mechanical boards clock at 2.1mm). Keyboard is hot swappable and you can change your magnetic switches really easily. Brightness and RGB is also good with no complaints in that department (you can customize it in the web software). The build quality is also good and think that board was upgraded to PBT switches since when typing on them the feel sandy and rough, sound quality is quite since magnetic switches are linear switches (both better in every way), and the keyboard is wired only which I prefer since I am using it on my personal PC and have no need to use it elsewhere. HE keyboards are definitely the future and every professional or enthusiast e-Sport gamer simply must have this keyboard because it gives them and edge in every way that mechanical keyboard simply cannot give at the moment! I recommended this board for anybody who is on the fence over coming to the HE world.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 24, 2026
review_body: After 17 years in the Apple ecosystem, I recently switched from an iPhone to a Samsung S26 Ultra so I needed a watch that worked with my new Android phone to replace my Apple Watch. I wasn't ready to throw down $300+ on a Galaxy Watch just yet so I looked for cheaper alternatives and that's when I found the Galaxy FIT 3. It does all of the major functions I need from a smart watch (time/date/temperature, fitness tracking, basic notifications, media playback controls). It comes with 100 different pre-set watch faces to customize your watch but they cannot be individually customized nor can any more be downloaded. The band is soft and comfortable (I'm not sure if there are many replacement bands to customize your FIT like are available for Apple Watches). The watch itself is much narrower vertically and lighter than my Apple Watch. I have to recharge it every 5-7 days (nowhere near the 14 day claimed battery life but much better than when I had to recharge my Apple Watch every day). It takes about 30 seconds per 1 percent to recharge the battery. The biggest downgrades from the Apple Watch or other higher end smartwatches is the smaller size of the display and its reduced scratch resistance (I've already gotten several small scratches on the watch face within the first month of use). But for under $50, it's well worth it, despite any shortcomings.

Only mildly sucks because I use the live feed heart rate monitor to help clue me in to if I might have a panic attack or if I'm overreacting. Another thing. I have been using google health to track my calories and set specific goals for some of my macros I'm trying to hit. Unfortunately, the samsung health app doesn't get this specific and just gives you the suggested daily intake as a metric rather than letting you set your own. What sucks more is that these two apps don't sync with each other. So now I have 2 seperate apps to track my health. All in all. Its really a fantastic little gadget. review_title: I can't believe the improvement over other switches. It's crazy!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on October 27, 2024
review_body: If you thought other companies made good key switches, then you are in for a surprise with this keyboard. Cherry absolutely nailed it with these new MX2A switches. I purchased the version with the Cherry MX2A Silent Red switches. Now, I basically hate linear switches. Really, I usually can't stand them, but these new silents reds are the smoothest, and most buttery feeling switches I have ever felt. I have been using mechanical keyboards my entire life. Since before the patent ran out on the Cherry MX switches and the only mechanical keyboards you could buy had Cherry switches. Now, everyone makes their own switches, with all kinds of "features" like hall effect, rapid trigger, analog, adjustable actuation, magnets, etc.. Here's the issue with all of those though, they feel like crap to type on and are super loud. I have spent thousands on keyboards over the years. I still have over 15 mechanical keyboards sitting in storage that I stopped using. I am not exaggerating either. To give you an idea of where I'm coming from, my favorite switches used to be Cherry MX Brown. Now they are Cherry MX2A Silent Reds. I haven't even mentioned how quiet they are too. Unbelievably quiet for a mechanical keyboard. It's definitely the quietest mech keyboard I have ever used, which is saying a lot. Some people may think the keyboard is fairly basic, and in all reality, it is. It doesn't require software, doesn't have RGB or any lights (besides the led for caps lock and such), it doesn't have a removeable cable, or a super high polling rate over 1000Hz. Visually and functionally speaking, the keyboard is simple. But that a huge positive in my book. It does have full N-key rollover, so if you do use it for gaming, there won't be any issues there. I don't need to install any bloat to use the keyboard. I don't need to configure anything. It's just plug and play. It's fairly compact for a full-sized keyboard too, so be aware of the slightly more compact layout. My only real complaint is that it does not have 4 rubber feet on the bottom to keep it from sliding around. There are 2 rubber feet on the bottom front, but on the bottom rear, the feet are hard plastic, so it doesn't stay in place super well. There are rubber pads on the bottom rear feet that fold out, but I don't use a keyboard angled, so they are useless for me. Other than that, one thing, this keyboard is perfect for me. Am I going to use it for my hardcore gaming sessions? No. I actually purchased it for office work, and it's going to be perfect for that. However, will I be purchasing another keyboard with these same exact switches for my gaming pc? 100% YES! Look, you may not like the design of this keyboard, or its simplicity, but do not sleep on these new Cherry switches. Cherry is back with a vengeance, and if you're looking for a new keyboard, get one with these new Cherry switches. Whether it be this keyboard or not. The switch is king, and Cherry is back on top.

review_title: Excellent watch functionality but some tweaks recommended
review_date: Reviewed in Australia on May 12, 2026
review_body: I had a sports watch and polar chest strap monitor 25 years ago for Concept 2 rower training. Technology has improved enormously since then. I chose the Garmin Forerunner 55 because I wanted simplicity as well as multi-functionality. It fulfils both needs. Above all the Garmin sports watch is accurate. I am now 71 and have just started training prep for another C25K with my daughter - hence the need for an accurate heart rate monitor. The things I like about the watch and app follow plus some suggested tweaks. On the positive side customisable heart rate zones are useful, and it is easy to develop warm up, walk, run, repeat x8 workouts, which can then be modified in subsequent weeks. However, I had to use AI to pose a dozen or so technical questions about how to set up specific procedures and to analyse and interpret some of the performance data that the Garmin produces. The written Garmin instructions in multiple languages don’t touch the sides of what the app can do hence using Google Gemini to pose detailed questions. Another user tip - the Garmin app can be integrated with the Chronometer app which monitors food and exercise expenditure. This combination of apps is a really sophisticated tool to record data, if you are of a scientific disposition. For example, if your Adjusted Baseline Activity hits zero, it indicates that your Garmin has accounted for every metabolic "tick" above your resting BMR. The wider screen of an Apple Mac is much more accessible to see all the post exercise Garmin data. The IPAD version of the Garmin app is actually a scaled mobile app and it is difficult to escape from a page as the menus are obscured. A workaround is to reset your IPad display to ‘more space’, but I would recommend using a laptop and the Garmin website which have no technical issues.

review_title: Great case, but watch your charging cable.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on December 14, 2025
review_body: I see the case has undergone a slight re-design since my original one. It come with in soft inner rubber shell with an outer hard rubber shell. I guess that's to better absorb impact. The original one they were molded together. Now the inner shell appears to be removeable. That said, it seems to be well made. It's a tight fit to get the phone in. The buttons line-up where they should, so they are functional. Someone mentioned in another review that they liked the dust cover for the charging port. For me, it's a a love/hate relationship. I love the idea of keeping it closed when not charging, but since the "hinge" part of the flap has a strong reflex to close, I have to keep my phone motionless while charging or the pressure the lid has will cause the cord to pop-out just enough to stop charging without visual queue to know it happened. I actually get better results on a cheaper and thinner cord, but then it wears out the cord faster. So, for sturdiness, I give this 5 stars. But overall, due the the aforementioned charging issue, I give it 4 stars. Also, the outer case is a bit slippery, I wish it had better hand grip material, but workable if you know that.

Overall this is a good watch! I did a lot of research and I would say if you're debating it just get it! It is far less expensive to try this and not like it and get something else then it is to try a $300-$800 watch that you hate but you already spent $$ so you feel stuck.

review_date: Reviewed in Australia on November 14, 2025
review_body: Im super impressed with the AMAZFIT BIP 6. I got it for my house mate as her FITBIT Versa 3 died on her. So i initially came across a YouTube review of this smart watch and it caught my eye being the tech nerd i am and i was super impressed, so i continued watching different reviews and they just got better and better so i recommended this to my house mate who knows NOTHING about tech lol, and we got it. Set up was SUPER easy and from set up i have got to say it has not missed a beat. It pretty much has got and does almost everything my 🍎 watch ultra 2 does, plus a few little things i like better, like you can set a time for AOD to turn on at 8am and turn off at 10pm i think this is awesome and it also puts the watch in to DND mode so it doesnt disturb you whilst your alseep. It has 4 or 5 standard AOD watch faces to chose from or you can use your actual chosen watch face for AOD. Has great fitness features and another thing i love is it has a toggle which you can press and ALL your stats come up without having to go into each one individually like HR, STRESS, FITNESS ( Activity) your breathing, etc. The Watch is Bluetooth of coarse and it has a super stable connection as mentioned has not disconnected once & has great range away from your phone, it can take calls and you can also make them. You can also send and recieve text messages and even has quick replies. The display i think is awesome can get super bright and no issues seeing details on a bright day. It actually gets so bright my housemate keeps it on the lowest level of brightness. It has all your toggles like DND, PING MY PHONE, TORCH, AirPlane Mode, etc. Its a really nice looking watch as well and this one we got is a beautiful colour. It takes just about most 22mm bands with quick release pins, so changing bands is easy and pretty much most 3rd party bands fit. The watch lasts a good 7 days if you dont have much activity going on and my house mate has been charging it up approx every 6 to 7 days, with more activity it will still last 4 to 5 days. My only little gripe is the battery charging puk, it doesnt come with a cable in the box. You have to be extremely careful not to loose the charging puc and also i been trying to look for a holder or stand for the puc and just cannot find one for the Bip 6 unless you spend a small fortune for the stand that fits the Puc made specifically which is a shame. She'd like to have some sort of puc stand so that she doesnt accidently loose the actual charger, would be nice if you could get your hands on more 3rd party ones ? Bar that this is an EXCELLENT smart watch and with my housemate using it over the last month or so she has been thoroughly impressed by it and so have i to be honest. Its also not that expensive for EVERYTHING this smart watch does plus more. If your looking for a good all round Andorid smart watch then this is the one, look no further, you will be pleasently surprised with it, if not overly. You can monitor your heart rate, blood oxygen levels, sleep, step count, weight, and more! It has a voice assistant and alarm clock as well. You can also sync most of your Apps on your paired device (I did my my phone), so that you can receive notifications and even use the same functions on your watch simultaneously. For example, I paired my youtube account so that whenever I receive a notification in the Youtube App of a new video, it shows that notification on my phone as well. I can even listen to YouTube using the play, pause, and stop buttons from my phone. I also synced our security camera device so that I can receive those notifications as well while away from home. I am able to select any number of applications I want to individually sync or not. This is great so that I can be selective and not have my watch going off every second of the day. It helps me to stay motivated as far as my fitness goes because I'm able to set goals - it sends you an achievement reward notification, which sounds once a goal has been reached. It has so many features that I haven't even begun to tap into. There is a slight learning curve, as with sny smart device, but it's very user-friendly after you patiently program and customize each feature to fit your needs and get the hang of it.

review_title: Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on August 1, 2026
review_body: I have tested numerous “smart watches” in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don’t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!)

review_title: Good quality, affordable mechanical keyboard. Surprised by its quality given its price range.
review_date: Reviewed in the United Kingdom on June 1, 2026
review_body: Very satisfied with this purchase. Head and shoulders above my membrane Logitech K120 Wired Business Keyboard, and without breaking the bank too! To be honest, I feel lucky to have gotten this keyboard at such a low price. At this price point, I could not find a single mechanical keyboard that met all of my requirements but this one. In fact, even some of the more expensive mechanical keyboards didn't meet all of my requirements. For starters, the keyboard uses the UK layout with the pound sign and hash symbol key in the right place—very important for me. Second, this is a full-size keyboard with a numeric keypad at the right. This was important for me as I wanted a keyboard that did all of the same things as my previous keyboard, the only difference being that it is mechanical—a requirement that this RisoPhy mechanical keyboard fulfils precisely. (I should note, too, that most of the mechanical keyboards at this price range and even some more expensive ones, being shorter in width, lacked a numeric keypad.) Then there is the feel of the keyboard. The product description says that it uses "BLUE switches", seemingly modelling its switches on the classic tactile and clicky Cherry MX Blue switches. (It is unlikely that the keyboard uses actual Cherry MX Blue switches, given the price range, but rather its own knock-off versions of the switches.) While this may not be what some gamers are looking for (looking for something smoother and offering the same resistance all the way down without a slight bump as you press each key), this is perfect for me, as I was looking for a keyboard that produced nice responsive, tactile feedback, mirroring a classic typewriter effect. Some people may be put off by this, thinking that it makes the keyboard too noisy, and while, yes, there is a clicking noise with each key press, it honestly isn't that loud (though because there is still an audible clicking noise, I can understand criticisms saying that this keyboard is inappropriate for an office environment, for example, where such a constant clicking noise can cause distractions.) The keyboard is nice to type on, which is my primary use for it rather than gaming.

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on November 18, 2018
review_body: This case looks much better in front of you than a picture can render. I have the Product Red iPhone XR and this is the red case. The color comes very close to the color of the aluminum frame and looks like part of the phone. At first glance it doesn't look like there is any case at all! The red color is a shiny, metallic red as opposed to the matte red color of the iPhone frame. It does not clash where the phone's color can be seen in the cutouts and it nicely compliments the color on the back of the phone! Contrary to what another reviewer said, this case does indeed have a lip for basic screen protection. If you lay your phone face down on a perfectly flat surface with this case on, the screen will not contact anything. That being said, it is minimal by design. If you think you may be tossing your expensive phone around in places where the screen could be impacted perhaps you would be better served with a more robust case. This case is a great value for what it is! It complements the phone's styling. It will protect your phone from scratches on the back and sides. I had an iPhone 6 Plus with no screen protector installed on the glass for four years. The only protection was the lip provided by the various cases I used. The glass never got more than the most superficial, barely visible marks in that length of time. Totally worth it to me for the arguably better user experience of the naked glass screen. Even the most pricey tempered glass screen protectors do not match the buttery smooth touchscreen experience in my opinion. My fingers do not slide the same way. Anyway, the glass on the iPhone XR is significantly tougher than previous phones and I don't anticipate a problem. I offer that information only to illustrate that, with proper care in handling, you can rock an inexpensive, minimalist case with no issues. It should be noted, as another reviewer has said, that the back of this case is NOT perfectly clear. The phone can be seen but there is a pattern or texture which is noticeable if you hold it to the light just right. Not a deal breaker at all for me. You can still showcase the beauty of your XR with this case but it could be an issue if you require a perfectly clear back. I think this pattern may have something to do with durability and I doubt it will be an issue to most users. There is a color coordinated lip to protect the camera lens and I love the custom color coordinated cutout for the flash and mic modules in the back. So many XR cases simply have a huge opening that looks like it was designed for a dual camera setup. I like the extra attention to detail. One caveat: The fit is snug. If you are like me and frequently take you case off for thorough cleaning or want to rock a different case for that day, care should be taken when removing this case. The iPhone's aluminum frame is slippery and you could launch your phone out of your hands! I bought several cases together to compare. The Ranvoo case is nearly identical to this one. That one is much easier to remove because it is ever so slightly thinner. It has the same attention to detail in the cutouts and the same pattern in the "clear" back. The tradeoff is there is virtually no raised lip to protect the screen which is why it's easier to remove. Both products are good for what they are. This Torras case is a remarkably nice product for the money. With proper care it could be the only case you need but at this price, it will be a nice option in your iPhone's wardrobe.

I also want to note that I have seen that this key board had gone a little viral on TikTok and I did purchase before it was trending so I would say if you are coming here from TikTok no, it’s not a scam it’s actually a great keyboard!

review_date: Reviewed in the United States on February 21, 2025
review_body: The Aula F99 is a "96%" mechanical keyboard that comes in around the $90 price point normally, but can get as low as $60 on sale. That form factor means that it does have a numpad and arrow keys as well as home, delete and page up/down keys, but those keys are moved up in-line with the function keys and the numpad/arrow keys are squished up closer to the main keys with the arrow keys set a little further down to make space. Having a numpad was a must for me because I like to play games that often use the numpad for important functions, and I also prefer typing numbers on a numpad when the occasion arises. At this price point, this is probably one of the best options for people who want a numpad and/or arrow keys but still want a keyboard that looks and sounds more like a custom keyboard you see in YouTube shorts of people doing sound tests.

The condensed layout takes a bit of getting used to, but that's true of any "less than 100%" sized keyboard. The only key that bothers me a bit in the layout is the "0" on the numpad, but I'm getting used to it. I haven't played with the lighting much, but it definitely helps visibility in low light. Bluetooth connection has been rock solid, and the battery life even with the lighting on has been phenomenal; after a few weeks of moderate use, I have yet to have to charge it. Overall I'm extremely happy with the purchase, highly recommend it... it's definitely a leader in "bang for buck" vs some of the higher priced brands!

review_title: Never thought I'd love a keyboard so much...
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on January 31, 2026
review_body: It's taking a little getting used to the slightly different arrangement of some keys but man... overall, this keyboard KICKS TAIL!!! I love how it lights up, I'm always working in low light or the dark and my eyes aren't what they used to be so I just can't tell you how much of a difference it makes. I also feel like the key symbols won't/can't wear out because they're backlit. Typical keyboards have letter and words wear off over time, but I don't see how that's possible with this keyboard. It's not a "gamer keyboard" it's just a great basic keyboard with all the functions you need. Keystrokes feel amazing! Not sure how to describe but when you're typing it just feels really nice. A real quality built product and worth every penny. I'm considering buying another before they don't make them anymore... LOL Oh, the battery lasts forever on this thing too. You can turn it OFF when you're done for the day and you can set the keyboard to pair/work with multiple computers (even have keys configured differently if you like). The backlight shuts off when you remove your hands from the keyboard or stop typing for about 5 seconds, but its got this really cool "motion detection" feature that once you put your hands over the keys again or start typing it lights right back up! I'm telling you if you're in the market for a new BLUETOOTH keyboard and are willing to pay a little more for a NICE one... this is the board to have!!! I really love it. I'll give you the 1 thing I didn't like about it as I began using it... The FUNCTION ROW of keys has no space above the NUMBERS or Number pad, etc. So it's super easy to hit the wrong keys sometimes. I'll often go to use the "home" key and end up hitting the key to switch between machines, or the biggest one is the "lock" key the farthest top right key over the number pad's "minus/dash" key. I often go to hit the "minus/dash" key and end up locking my windows (having to sign in again). HOWEVER, using the Logitech software that is used to configure the keyboard I was able to just disable that lock key. I don't need a KEY for that anyway. When I want to lock my Windows session (log out) without shutting down, I'll just do it the normal way with my mouse (Start > Power > Lock). No big, been doing that forever anyway. Anyway, this keyboard is awesome. Especially, once you get used to it. Most times I get a new keyboard and have to get used to the key arrangements and different spacing anyway. Might as well do it with a great keyboard. 😊👍🏻 P.S. I have always been a Microsoft keyboard/mouse kinda guy. I didn't think much of Logitech until I got the MX Master 2 Mouse, which is now also my favorite ever. This keyboard goes with that mouse it's sold in bundles they're of the same product set.

review_title: Works Great with Windows and Ubuntu/Linux
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on December 21, 2020
review_body: I have had no issues running this with my work laptop HP Laptop running Windows 10 and my Dell Inspiron 17 running Ubuntu 20.10/Windows 10. Both laptops charge, and all ports seem to work well. In general, the worst part of the USB-C format is the confusing amount of different laptops that seem to implement it in different ways. Not this product's fault; as I said, it works well with Dell and HP while my HP Laptop dock runs with both laptops, but under Ubuntu or Windows 10 on my Dell, it falls short. The HP Dock is a Thunderbolt dock, and my Dell is a Display port marked with a DP; the DP Port on my Dell does charge and allows all ports to work with this dock. I mention it because USB-C gets confusing, and mileage may vary depending on the laptop itself. My Hp is marked as Thunderbolt, and my Dell as Display Port, and this product runs wonderfully with both. I found I could get a 4k Display using the DP port on the back of the dock in Ubuntu, but I found it a little problem some and instead switched to using the two HDMI ports instead. Sometimes 4k would flicker, but that can be my older KVM Switch (1080P KVM). I don't mind the two 1080p screens as the dock makes it so easy to switch computers. I wonder why the HDMI port only seems to pump out 1080P and the display port 4k from my experience. Still, my HP dock didn't do 4k at all, so this dock outperformed it. I have even booted my Dell and HP Laptops with a live USB of MX Linux, and with no configuration, it worked. I just changed the display settings a bit.

review_title: Cheap switches you will have to replace. I wish Asus would have done better with this product.
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on May 14, 2026
review_body: Here is the deal I have with this mouse: brand new out of the box and already have double-clicking going on. Two weeks of use. While they do include a spare set of switches, this still does not account for the fact they are cheap. No wonder it's designed so one can replace switches so easily. For the price, Asus should be ASHAMED. For me, I just ordered proper switches to replace what this product came with. Not a big deal as they are dirt cheap. But still, as I stated, for a $100+ mouse, the switches should not be this cheap. This is a heavy mouse. If you use a cloth mouse pad, you are not going to like this mouse. You feel the friction and the weight of this mouse on this material. I switched to my Logitech G440 hard-covered mouse pad, and it slides like a dream. I was going to order glass skates. Glad I did not. If you install new states, you will be unable to use the dock mount. I do like the fact that there are 6 side buttons. Using a glass mouse pad or hard cover allows me to play FPS games with ease. I like the 5 DPI settings, but, again, for the price, they could have added a few more possibilities. For a few dollars more, you can have a G502 with superior hardware but a lack of side buttons. I operate in an entire Asus ecosystem; I have an Asus motherboard, PSU, AIO cooler, 5080 GPU, & 3 monitors, so I already have Armory Crate installed on my system. If you buy this mouse, you HAVE to install Armory Crate to make use of this mouse in any good way. That being said, Armory Crate is notorious for being known as bloatware. Which, in my opinion, it is. There's really no need for it to be running and eating up system resources like this app does. So buyer beware. I would have brought a Razer instead, but that mouse too requires that you install their software to work their mouse. The lesser of two evils for me was this mouse. The construction, meaning the mouse shapes and material, feels robust and tank-like. But I dare not drop it. It feels like a smartphone: it looks built for durability and day-to-day use, but one drop and it's broken. Mainly because of the weight of this mouse. It's like dropping a brick from 2'. So take care of your equipment or at least get the protection. I know this review sounds bad, but it's really not. I do enjoy this mouse; I like the fit in my hand (I have mid-size hands), I love the ring finger resting point, and the scroll wheel is smooth. My issues are stated: It should come with better switches; one needs a hard surface area to really be able to move this mouse without muscle failure, and the bloatware just to use this. It should be a $60 mouse, because in the end, you will be buying upgraded switches and looking for a mouse pad that will work well with this mouse. As far as gameplay, it does take some getting used to, but it's doable. Back in the day, gamers used to play FPS with ball mice. While this is 1000% better, a lightweight/gamer mouse would be a better pick. The 6 side buttons are the lifesaver for this mouse for me. While it takes a little time to set up profiles so they do work in the games you are playing, once it's done, you are golden. Windows does not support any more than, like, 3 or 4 side buttons, so you have to program the unsupported ones to bind to keys, then in-game, bind that key to your mouse. All in all, a good, solid mouse as long as you don't mind the 'little' headaches that come along with it. 3 stars because there are better mice out there & for a company like Asus, I would expect better from them.

review_title: Read this if you are having issues
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on February 27, 2025
review_body: I bought this a while back and while shopping for a second dock for my wife, I came across a lot of reviews where people are complaining about this thing. I relate to those experiences, but the problem is not the dock itself. Mine worked at first and then it started to work intermittently. Sometimes, my external monitor would come on and sometimes it wouldn't. I tried it with different Anker cables (I had been using the one that came with it) and I even tried it with different Macbooks. At one point, I actually thought the problem was probably with Apple. It was really frustrating and annoying. But then I decided to try a new Thunderbolt 4 cable I had purchased from Cable Matters. I didn't really expect that to make a difference, but it solved everything. It has worked perfectly for over a year now. I connect my laptop and I can instantly use my monitor and get to work without a hassle. I've since realized that while Anker makes good power bricks and even hubs, they make really crappy cables. I have a LOT of them, unfortunately. They short out very quickly and I've noticed they often separate near the connectors. For stuff like lightning cables, you know right away when it stops working. But Thunderbolt cables can be confusing because they don't just fail. A bad cable will work really well sometimes and then not at all other times. It doesn't make sense that you would get perfect resolution on your monitor one day and not even be able to get it to turn on the next. For high bandwidth like 4K external monitors, you really just need a high quality, reliable cable. Don't try to save money on that and don't buy cables from Anker. I hope this is helpful to people.

review_body: My go-to earbuds have been the Powerbeats 3 for many years. I love the fullness of the sound, although the high-mids can lack some clarity. Last year I decided to get full wireless earbuds and thought I would give one of the cheaper alternatives a try. I got the Tozo T6, and ended up liking them quite a bit. Recently I got the Tozo NC9 to see if there is any improvement, and besides, they are so inexpensive! After tweaking these a fair amount, I finally got a sound I really like that is comparable to the Powerbeats 3. Soundwise, these are not much different from the T6, though I think the T6 have a little more low end out-of-the-box, but this can be adjusted with EQ. The NC9s fit in the ear more comfortably and the ear tips do not protrude as far down into the ear canal. The NC9s practically disappear into the ear and don't have the telltale tail hanging out like Apple AirPods. The NC9s do have noise cancelling, but that is not a feature that I care that much about, so I won't comment on it. I normally wear these on my morning walk or jog.

review_title: Durable, great noise canceling, great sound quality
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on June 17, 2026
review_body: I own three pairs of these earbuds in different colors (black, red, sage green) that I've bought over time and keep in different places for different uses. One pair for using while at work, one pair in my bedroom for connecting to my laptop or TV, one pair that I use while riding my motorcycle. The noise canceling on these is fantastic for the price. The helmet I use for riding does have a bit of a wind noise problem and my bike doesn't have a windshield, but while wearing these earbuds on NC mode going 50 mph down the road, I couldn't hear the wind at all, and the music quality is great. I've been a fan of Tozo earbuds for quite a while (used to use the T6s) but this specific model has been my favorite, ESPECIALLY for the great price that they're at. They do stick out of my ears a little bit further than I'd like, which makes getting a helmet on and off with them in very difficult, but obviously these aren't actually intended to be motorcycle ear plugs so that may just be me being picky. I've never had complaints about the sound quality, though I've never tried using them during a phone call so I can't speak to their performance there. I have dropped the earbuds on the ground several times while at work from pretty high up and they have yet to break. I'm a butcher so there's always water and beef blood on the floor, which I've dropped them in, and they still work fine. I lost one of the buds inside a meat freezer for a couple hours and upon retrieving it, it was still working perfectly fine. I don't know how Tozo sells these buds for so cheap when in my experience they are absolute tanks of earbuds. They don't fall out of my ears so all of the dropping was entirely my own fault. Once I put them in I very rarely have to worry about them falling out. If all three of my pairs somehow got lost or ruined, I wouldn't hesitate to order another three to replace them.

review_title: Pleasantly surprised how good it is
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on June 30, 2025
review_body: For years I have been a fan of the Razer Viper series. I've had a wired version, and now 3 of the original wireless Viper ultimate's, and now this one. I liked the wireless so much even though my wired version still works I bought the first 2 ultimate's to replace it. This is so I had one at home and one at work. Well I lost one of them on a work trip and after years one of them stopped worked (not sure what happened) but it was pretty old at that point). I keep buying the old ultimate version because I like the side grips and don't mind the slight weight increase they bring. The old version is typically cheaper than the newer one anyway and I don't mind the slight weight increase it probably brings. While this version is slightly heavier than my old ultimate and doesn't have the side grips. It's still lighter than many mice out there and still easy to pick up without the side grips. I will spend a little more for the ultimate for my home mouse because I still like it better and it is lighter weight. But for work this is more than sufficient and was much cheaper. The viper series has been known to be one of the top rated mice on the market for years and I will continue to buy it for years to come. Also I don't care about the RGB so its nice this one doesn't come with any. The only downside of that is that its harder to tell when its low on battery. Guess you could say its a double edged sword. The only downside I have to this mouse is I think they removed the side buttons on the right which I frequently used to refresh web pages. But I don't feel the need to do that as often as I used to so I think its a compromise I am willing to make here especially for the price. This is still the most comfortable mice I've ever used, super smooth tracking, built quality is good, and you don't have holes in the mouse which would allow dust to build up inside (let alone if you spilled something in there or had food on your hands. review_body: I gave this mouse 5 stars simply because of the haptic triggers. Ive only ever used the razer viper pro mouse and for my large hands its the only one that fits comfortably. The superstrike is a bit smaller in my hand but nothing that would make me stop using it. Its heavier than the razer and to my surprise I actually like and prefer that. The battery life on the mouse is great. The settings you choose for the haptic triggers does affect battery life but its nothing major. Now the main reason I bought this mouse was for the haptic system it uses and ill be blunt and say its the best thing ever and I hope more companies adapt this. Being able to adjust the actuation points is fantastic. It will take a few days to get used to the sensitivity if you go all the way to one but once youre used to it you'll never want a regular mouse again. Overall I think its a fantastic mouse its a bit spendy but in my opinion the haptic system by itself is worth the price. The only issue i have with this mouse is the side buttons they are extremely squishy they barely click its very unsatisfying I would give the side buttons a half a star.

review_title: Best haptic-inductive trigger wireless lightspeed gaming mouse ever!
review_date: Reviewed in the United States on February 17, 2026
review_body: I'm so impressed that click latency and feedback feels much faster than traditional mechanical switches. Yes, you can tweak it via Logitech G Hub to adjust rapid trigger, haptic click, and trigger latency. As soon as I set to 0 for haptic click, it feels noticeably faster and I can CPS (Clicks Per Second) much faster nowadays, especially in Counter-Strike 2, and other competitive multiplayer game. In addition, mouse weight is 61g which still feels light, not hefty. Durability and material feels high-quality, not too mush, no rattles, no problem whatsoever. However, it comes to pricing, yes it is unfortunately expensive at a price of $179.99 USD, but hey, you pay what you get for value and performance. All in all, this is such a huge game changer and this is definitely going to change the meta when it comes to gaming tournament e-sport!
